# Backend Conventions

## Async Safety
- **MinIO calls MUST use `asyncio.to_thread()`** in async endpoints. MinIO client is sync (urllib3). Direct calls block event loop; when MinIO is unreachable, blocks ALL requests for 30+s. Client configured with short timeouts (connect=5s, read=10s, 2 retries)
- **Celery uses sync DB** (`psycopg`), API uses async (`asyncpg`). Never mix.

## Credits & Billing
- **Two-stage debit**: ① Pre-check balance (402 if insufficient) → ② `debit_credits()` pre-debits estimated cost (returns ledger ID) → stream → `reconcile_credits()` UPDATEs same ledger entry to actual cost. Single ledger record per chat. LLM failure → DELETE entry + full refund
- **`ChatRequest` exposes only `mode` field** (`quick`/`balanced`; legacy `thorough` is retired). `model` field removed — prevents billing bypass
- Stripe webhook: `checkout.session.completed` for subscriptions only updates plan (no credits); `invoice.payment_succeeded` grants monthly credits (idempotent by invoice.id)
- `POST /api/billing/cancel` is self-serve and records optional `cancel_reason`, `cancel_feedback`, and `refund_requested` metadata in `plan_transitions`. `refund_requested` is an internal review flag; do not issue Stripe refunds from this path unless an explicit refund workflow is added.

## Parse Worker
- `time_limit=600`, `soft_time_limit=540`, `autoretry_for=(Exception,)`, max 2 retries, 60s backoff
- Idempotent re-parse: **delete Qdrant vectors (by `document_id` filter) BEFORE deleting DB pages/chunks**. Ordering matters — a Qdrant outage must leave the existing rows intact (set error + return), else the two stores diverge / data is lost. Then re-index.
- **OCR trigger = `detect_scanned` (no text layer) OR `detect_low_quality_text` (PDF text layer present but garbled — broken-font cmap, Unicode-aware quality score)**. R2b fix for docs like U13 that have garbage text and so were never detected as "scanned".
- **OCR language is content-based**: `detect_script_osd` runs `tesseract --psm 0` (OSD) on sample pages → `resolve_ocr_languages(locale, script)` returns a NARROW set (script family, ≤3, **no `eng` for non-Latin** — it injects Latin noise). Never the kitchen-sink set (causes cross-script hallucination); locale only refines within a script family. Adopt a low-quality re-OCR only if it beats the text-layer quality. Persist `parse_version`/`parse_method`/`text_quality`/`ocr_languages` on the doc.
- Backfill stale/low-quality docs with `scripts/find_low_quality_docs.py` (skips `parse_version>=current` unless `--force`).

## Auth
- **`FOR UPDATE` lock** on verification tokens to prevent TOCTOU
- Internal Auth Adapter API uses `X-Adapter-Secret` header

## Error Handling
- Use `HTTPException` (not `JSONResponse`) for all non-SSE endpoints
- Lifespan pattern (`@asynccontextmanager`) instead of deprecated `@app.on_event`

## Demo System
- 3 seed PDFs auto-deployed at startup from `backend/seed_data/`. Self-healing: detects Qdrant data loss → full re-seed
- Anonymous: 5 msgs/session, 500 sessions/doc, 10 req/min/IP, forced DeepSeek V4 Flash
- Logged-in users accessing demo docs use their credits with no message limit

# Frontend Conventions

## Architecture
- **All pages are `"use client"`** — client components with server wrapper for metadata
- Pages that fetch API data must render meaningful content in loading AND error states (prevents Google Soft 404)

## API Proxy
- **ALL** frontend→backend calls go through `/api/proxy/*` route, which injects JWT. Including SSE chat stream (`sse.ts`). Missing this = 401 errors
- **JWT double-layer**: Auth.js uses encrypted JWE (unreadable by backend). Proxy creates plain HS256 JWT via `jose`. Backend `deps.py` validates exp/iat/sub
- `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking: true` enables cross-provider auto-linking by email
- **Proxy maxDuration**: `route.ts` exports `maxDuration = 60` (Vercel Hobby limit). SSE chat 60s timeout, others 30s

## UI Design System
- **Palette (app UI)**: zinc monochrome + blue accent (`#1D4ED8`/`#60A5FA`). Zero `gray-*`/`indigo-*`/`violet-*`/`purple-*` classes (except Google OAuth brand + status colors). Zero `transition-all` (use specific properties)
- **Editorial marketing layer**: the entire public marketing surface (unauthenticated `/`, `use-cases/*`, `compare/*`, `alternatives/*`, `features/*`, `tools/*`, `pricing`, `trust`, `demo`) uses a SEPARATE scoped editorial design system — `frontend/src/app/editorial.css` (every rule under `.dt-editorial`), a warm-paper palette (`--ed-paper`/`--ed-ink`/`--ed-signal` terracotta `#b0472f`/`--ed-ochre`) with Newsreader serif + IBM Plex Mono fonts, **light-only**. It does NOT use the zinc/blue app palette. **Design decision locked 2026-05-20**: the product runs on TWO surface treatments (editorial marketing terracotta+warm-paper vs functional app zinc+blue) sharing one token base (logo, body font Inter, spacing scale, micro-interactions). A blue-accent unification was tried and reverted because the warm-paper terracotta identity is load-bearing. Do not re-propose merging the accents. Marketing pages compose the shared editorial kit in `frontend/src/components/marketing/` (`MarketingShell`, `EditorialMarketingHeader`, `EdPageHero`, `EdSection`, `EdProse`, `EdFeatureList`, `EdCardGrid`, `EdStepRow`, `EdFaqList`, `EdCtaBanner`, `EdComparisonTable`, `EdInlineCell`, `EdRelatedLinks`, `EdCheckList`, `EdChoiceList`) — `MarketingShell` supplies the `.dt-editorial` root, so kit components never add it themselves. Keep editorial styles scoped under `.dt-editorial`; do not let them leak into the functional app UI, and do not apply the zinc/blue rule to editorial components. Pages still on the zinc/blue app palette: `about`, `contact`, `imprint`, `privacy`, `terms`, `blog/*`, `document-diff` (not yet editorialized).
- **i18n**: Components using `t()` MUST be inside `<LocaleProvider>`. Outside = raw key fallback. Only `en` is statically loaded; other 10 locales lazy-loaded

## PDF & Documents
- **react-pdf v9 CJK**: After upgrading react-pdf/pdfjs-dist, MUST re-copy `cmaps/`, `standard_fonts/`, `pdf.worker.min.mjs` to `public/`. Worker loaded from same-origin (not CDN) for CSP compliance
- **bbox coordinates**: Normalized [0,1], top-left origin. Three citation highlight strategies: ① PDF bbox, ② TextViewer text-snippet match, ③ converted PDF fallback to text-snippet when dummy bbox detected

## Subscriptions & Feature Gating
- Free (300/mo) + Plus (3K/mo, $9.99) + Pro (9K/mo, $19.99). Annual = 20% discount
- Visible modes are Flash and Pro. Internal IDs remain `quick` and `balanced`; retired modes such as `thorough` must migrate to Flash.
- Free includes Flash plus a capped number of Pro answers/month. Export: Plus+ (frontend gated). Custom Instructions: Pro (backend gated). Sessions: Free=3/doc (backend gated)
- Credit packs: Boost(500/$3.99), Power(2K/$9.99), Ultra(5K/$19.99)
- Cancellation UI must remain self-serve. The cancel form may collect an optional reason, optional feedback, and a refund-review checkbox, but it must not block cancellation on those fields.

# Quote Finder + Evidence Board — Design Plan (Round 1)

**Date:** 2026-06-12
**Author:** Claude (research-backed; 3 parallel research streams: verbatim-quote tech, citation-formatting tech, codebase audit)
**Status:** ROUND 3 — CONSENSUS CANDIDATE. Codex r1 (`.collab/reviews/2026-06-12-quote-finder-codex-r1.md`) + r2 (`...-codex-r2.md`) findings ACCEPTED in full; resolutions in §8 below override conflicting text in D1–D8/§5. Dialogue: `.collab/dialogue/2026-06-12-quote-finder-r1.md`.
**Goal:** First real paying users. Strategy ratified from production Q&A analysis (2026-06-12): the best-retained organic users are thesis writers extracting verbatim quotes + page numbers from their PDFs (users bas\*\*\*, mel\*\*\*, ric\*\*\*, mca\*\*\* — the ONLY multi-week-retention cohort in the entire DB). Build the workflow they are hand-rolling through chat today.

**Explicitly OUT of scope (owner decision 2026-06-12):** lifecycle/re-engagement emails of any kind.

---

## 1. Product shape

1. **Quote Finder** — a deliberate action on a document (and later collection): user enters a topic ("translator invisibility caused by fluency"), gets back a list of **machine-verified verbatim quote cards**: exact source text, page number, jump-to-highlight, one-click copy as APA/MLA/Chicago in-text citation with page locator.
2. **Evidence Board** — saved quotes persist per document/user with note field; export quote bank as DOCX / BibTeX / RIS (Plus-gated).
3. **Monetization**: quote search costs credits like a chat message (two-stage debit, existing); saving quotes is the habit hook — Free caps at `FREE_SAVED_QUOTES_LIMIT=20`; exports (DOCX/BibTeX/RIS) ride the existing Plus export gate.
4. **Trust contract (the differentiator)**: a quote card is NEVER shown unless the server verified the text verbatim against the stored page text. Competitive research confirms no incumbent (Scite/Elicit/SciSpace/Anthropic Citations) guarantees verbatim quotes + page + sub-page highlight from the user's own PDF.

## 2. Architecture decisions (research-grounded — do not re-litigate without new evidence)

### D1. Verbatim guarantee: "LLM proposes, verifier disposes, source displays" (REVISED r2)
Pattern from Deterministic Quoting (healthcare RAG) + Google LangExtract + Anthropic Citations API design.

> **r1 correction (Codex catch, prod-verified 2026-06-12):** `pages.content` is **NULL for ALL PDF pages** (9,243/9,243 in prod; `parse_worker.py:214-239` populates `extracted_content_map` only in the `file_type != "pdf"` branch). The original "verify against raw page text" design had no verification target for the dominant format. Revised as follows.

- DeepSeek only *proposes* quotes (JSON: `{quote_text, source_ref_n, page}`), with abstention licensed in the prompt ("if no relevant quotes exist, return []" — Anthropic's documented quotes-first pattern).
- Server-side **verification gate** locates each proposed quote in **`chunks.text` of the cited chunk (± retrieved neighbors)** — the exact text the LLM saw, already in Postgres for every document and format:
  - **Tier 1**: exact substring in the cited chunk's text → `exact`.
  - **Tier 2**: exact substring in normalized space, projected back to chunk-text offsets via an index-preserving offset map → `normalized`.
  - **Tier 3**: `rapidfuzz.fuzz.partial_ratio_alignment(quote_norm, chunk_norm, score_cutoff=90)`; auto-accept ≥95 with length-ratio sanity check → `aligned`. 90–95 → flagged, not auto-shown.
  - Below cutoff or ref cross-check mismatch → **dropped** (counted, shown as "n verified, m discarded").
  - **Displayed text is ALWAYS the chunk-text slice — never the LLM emission.** The guarantee becomes "verbatim w.r.t. our stored extraction", whose cleaning (header/footer strip, dehyphenation, whitespace collapse) matches what PDF copy-paste produces; the one-click bbox jump lets the user eyeball the original instantly.
  - **Dedup**: 50-token chunk overlap means one quote can verify in two chunks → dedupe by (normalized quote text, page).
- **Fidelity upgrade path (same release, forward-only):** parse_worker starts persisting raw per-page text for PDFs into `pages.content` (capture `page.get_text()` in the existing extract pass; trivial). New uploads then get page-level Tier-1 verification + page-grounded display; old docs stay on chunk-level verification. No mass re-parse, no lazy MinIO fetch in v1.
- Page disambiguation for repeated phrases: trust the cited chunk's `page_start/page_end`; cross-chunk duplicates resolved by dedup rule above.
- Docs where `text_quality` is present AND < 0.75 (doc-level nullable column, migration 0032): cap at flagged tier, never auto-accept Tier 3. NULL `text_quality` (pre-R2b docs) = no cap (text-layer docs), but `parse_method='ocr'` without quality always caps.
- **New dependency: `rapidfuzz`** (C++, the same migration Google made for LangExtract; provides score-AND-locate in one call). `edlib` deferred — YAGNI for v1.

### D2. Normalization pipeline (shared, index-preserving)
NFKC → strip soft hyphen U+00AD + tatweel U+0640 → fold curly quotes/dashes/ellipsis + CJK fullwidth/corner quotes 「」『』 → rejoin line-break hyphenation → collapse whitespace (incl. NBSP, U+3000) → casefold (fuzzy tier only). Arabic extra: strip Mn (tashkeel), normalize alef/hamza set. CJK: character-level matching everywhere, no word tokenization. Both sides (LLM quote AND page text) run the identical pipeline; matching happens in normalized space; results project back through the offset map.

### D3. bbox/highlight: reuse, don't rebuild (CLARIFIED r2)
Verified r1: chunks store **line-level** normalized bboxes (JSONB list with page; `parse_service.py:834` "line-level bbox precision", accumulated at `:790`), and `chat_service.py:203-260` already assembles the citation payload `{chunk_id, page, page_end, bboxes, snippet, ...}` from them; frontend has 3 highlight strategies incl. text-snippet fallback. Quote cards emit the same citation payload shape: bboxes = the cited chunk's line bboxes for the quote's page; frontend `findSnippetInPage(verifiedSlice)` narrows to the quote. **No parse-pipeline change required for highlight; works on all existing docs.**

### D4. Retrieval: reuse hybrid + over-retrieve
Existing stack (semantic Qdrant + lexical ILIKE + RRF + dynamic top_k) is sufficient for v1; quote queries are recall-bound → boost top_k for quote searches (~2× chat). Postgres FTS/pg_trgm is a known gap — deferred unless replay shows recall failures.

### D5. Citation formatting: citeproc-py, not Node, not hand-rolled
- `citeproc-py` 0.9.3 (Apr 2026, active; used in production by Zenodo via `citeproc-py-styles`) + official CSL styles: APA 7, MLA 9, Chicago author-date. Supports page locators (`Locator('page','17')`) → "(Venuti, 1995, p. 17)".
- Known gap: no year-suffix disambiguation (1995a/1995b) → deterministic 20-line pre-pass (group by author+year, append suffix).
- Correctness contract: golden snapshot tests vs Zotero-generated output for ~10 representative items.
- Fallback: per-style template functions behind the same `format_citation(item, style) -> (in_text, bibliography)` interface.
- Rejected: citeproc-js/citation-js (Node sidecar = new infra, AGPL concerns), pandoc binary (~100MB, shell-out), full hand-roll (multi-author/title-case/et-al rules are deceptively expensive for an audience that will notice errors).

### D6. Bibliographic metadata: Zotero's hybrid pattern, no GROBID
1. PyMuPDF doc metadata + first 2–3 pages text (already in `pages.content`).
2. Regex scan ~first 80 lines for DOI / ISBN / arXiv ID → Crossref `works/{doi}` (polite pool, `mailto=`) / OpenLibrary (1 rps anon → identified UA).
3. No identifier → DeepSeek structured extraction (JSON plumbing exists in extraction feature).
4. Optional Crossref `query.bibliographic` verify (accept top hit only above title-similarity threshold).
5. **Always lands in a user-editable form** (Zotero's UX); cached per document (`document_biblio` table, CSL-JSON + source flag).
- Rejected: GROBID (8GB Docker/Java service, accuracy validated on scholarly articles not books; new Railway infra for a solo dev).

### D7. Exports
- DOCX quote bank: `python-docx` (already a dep), extend existing `export_service.py` + reuse `_sanitize_xml_text`.
- BibTeX: hand-rolled writer (~50 lines; bibtexparser v2 still beta and we only generate).
- RIS: hand-rolled writer (~half day) — imports into Zotero/Mendeley/EndNote; cheap differentiator. Zotero Web API push deferred to v2.

### D8. Data model (Alembic after 20260524_0032)
```
saved_quotes: id uuid pk, user_id fk, document_id fk, page int,
  quote_text text (raw slice), bboxes jsonb, verification_tier text,
  note text null, created_at, updated_at
document_biblio: document_id pk fk, csl_json jsonb, source text
  ('identifier'|'llm'|'user'), updated_at
```

## 3. Funnel fixes bundled (week 1, no emails)
- **Activation-collapse investigation**: 16/19 post-05-24 signups never uploaded (was 56%); 116 magic-link requests → ~19 signups in 19 days. Instrument signup→first-upload path, audit SEO locale-page entry UX, verify magic-link completion on prod. Diagnostic first; fixes follow evidence.
- **Restore document-generated suggested questions** (backend still populates `documents.suggested_questions`; commit 6693342 removed display). Restore ONLY the per-document generated ones, not the generic hardcoded list.
- **Move the paywall off the upload gate**: FREE max file size 25→50MB (config). The single historical payer paid at this gate *before experiencing value* and churned same day.
- Verify Stripe plan→credits mapping with a test-mode purchase (suspected +300-instead-of-3000 from 05-23 retro; current code reads correct).

## 4. Acquisition (week 4, code-only)
Programmatic SEO tool pages on the existing Phase-A locale-URL + editorial-kit pattern: `tools/pdf-quote-finder`, `tools/citation-from-pdf` (× 11 locales). Demo doc: add a theory-book PDF with a prefilled quote-finder example (current demo set skews finance; organic users are academic).

## 5. Sequencing
- **W1**: funnel fixes + `quote_verification_service` (normalization + 3-tier gate, TDD — this is the riskiest pure-logic component, fully unit-testable).
- **W2**: Quote Finder endpoint + retrieval boost + DeepSeek JSON prompt + quote-card UI w/ jump-to-highlight + copy-citation (in-text only, biblio service stub).
- **W3**: Evidence Board (tables, CRUD, board UI, caps) + biblio pipeline + citeproc-py wrapper + exports (DOCX/BibTeX/RIS, Plus gate).
- **W4**: SEO tool pages + demo doc + polish + in-prod replay vs the real user queries (bas\*\*\*/mel\*\*\*/ric\*\*\*/mca\*\*\* query corpus as acceptance tests).

## 6. Known risks / failure modes
- DeepSeek JSON adherence (mitigated: existing extraction JSON plumbing + retry-on-parse-fail).
- Hallucinated source refs (mitigated: ref range-validation + echoed-text cross-check — double signal).
- Quote recall too low on big docs → over-retrieve; if replay shows misses, add pg_trgm phrase search (explicitly deferred, not forgotten).
- OCR/garbled pages → text_quality cap (D1).
- citeproc-py style bugs → snapshot tests + per-style fallback templates (D5).
- Crossref/OpenLibrary offline → pipeline degrades to LLM extraction + user edit (D6 order is graceful).

## 7. Open questions — RESOLVED r2 (Claude positions amended by Codex r1+r2; final form in §8.4)
1. **Credit pricing of a quote search → chat-style token two-stage debit** (predebit 15 like balanced, reconcile to actual). It is one LLM call over retrieved context — same cost shape as chat; flat extraction-style predebit (`EXTRACTION_PREDEBIT_CREDITS` precedent, `extractions.py:213`) overcharges short docs and is reserved for multi-call jobs.
2. **`FREE_SAVED_QUOTES_LIMIT=20` on LIVE board count** (deleting frees a slot) — matches the "3 active share links" free-cap precedent (`sharing.py:85`). 20 ≈ one seminar paper's evidence, less than a thesis chapter — right pressure point.
3. **Chat routing: keep chat untouched in v1.** When the existing query router detects quote intent in a chat message, render a non-blocking "Try Quote Finder" chip above the answer (UI only, zero chat-pipeline risk). Auto-rerouting deferred to v1.1 — silent behavior changes in chat were the source of past regressions (R2a router gate history).
4. **`document_biblio` separate table** — documents is already wide; biblio has its own lifecycle + source flag; precedent: extraction results live in their own table joined to DocumentJob.
5. **Tier-3 thresholds stand (95 auto / 90–95 flagged).** With chunk-side display (r2 revision) a false-accept can no longer corrupt *wording* — only *attribution* — so the threshold guards location accuracy; stricter-than-LangExtract remains correct because our claim is a guarantee, not best-effort extraction.

## 8. Round-2 consensus resolutions (ACCEPTED from Codex r1+r2 — these override conflicting text above)

### 8.1 Verification substrate preconditions (amends D1/D2)
The chunk pipeline is a sound anti-hallucination gate but NOT yet a verbatim-display substrate. Before any quote card renders chunk text:
- **Fix sentence-split mutation**: `_split_into_sentences` (parse_service.py:893-906) + strip/rejoin (:482-487, :765-782) corrupts `U.S.`→`U. S.`, `3.14`→`3. 14`. Chunk display text must come from offset-preserving slices of cleaned block text, or splitting gets abbreviation/decimal guards. Fidelity tests required: `U.S.`, `e.g.`, decimals, DOI strings.
- **Fix hard-hyphen loss**: `_extract_line_blocks` (:855-864) turns `cost-\neffective` into `costeffective`. Mark line-break hyphen joins in an offset map (preserve/restore when ambiguous); tests for discretionary vs compound hyphens.
- **Persist PDF page text forward-only** (`page.get_text("text")` per page) AND store verification anchors on saved quotes: `source_chunk_id`, char offsets, `page_text_hash`, `quote_hash` — saved quotes must survive/revalidate after reparses.
- **Page derivation from the verified slice, not the LLM emission.** For `page_start≠page_end` chunks there is no offset→page map (tables.py:140-145): page-scoped verification where `pages.content` exists; chunk-fallback must reject or split ambiguous multi-page matches.
- **Dedup key**: `(document_id, normalized_quote_text, verified_page_range, start_offset-or-bbox-signature)` — not `(text, page)`.
- **Fuzzy guards**: tier-3 auto-accept additionally requires quote ≥ ~8 tokens / 40 chars, sane length ratio, match within the cited chunk/page window, and clean `text_quality`; short quotes / OCR / `text_quality<0.75` → exact/normalized only or flagged.
- **Honest trust labels**: chunk-fallback docs say "verified against extracted text"; only page-text-verified docs say "verified against page text". Quote Finder misses headings/headers/tables by construction (cleaning strips them) — say so in UI copy.

### 8.2 Highlight (amends D3 — Codex r1 verdict BLOCK accepted)
Persisted bboxes are bare `{page,x,y,w,h}` rects with no offsets/text (parse_service.py:526-530, :936-942) — span-level selection is impossible without reconstruction, and the PDF snippet-fallback only fires on all-dummy bboxes (PageWithHighlights.tsx:64-77).
- v1: emit the cited chunk's bboxes for the verified page, **label highlight precision as approximate**, store `source_chunk_id` + quote span offsets for future precision.
- Frontend change: allow a verified quote to snippet-highlight on the PDF text layer even when bboxes are present-but-coarse (extend, don't bend, the dummy-bbox path).
- Span-to-bbox word mapper (PyMuPDF reopen) = fast-follow, not v1.

### 8.3 Retrieval (amends D4)
Over-retrieve alone is insufficient (24-chunk cap, corrective_retrieval_service.py:92-114; lexical = ILIKE only). v1 adds deterministic candidate expansion: normalized phrase/term scan over the document's chunks (and page text where present) merged into candidates before generation. Telemetry per search: `retrieved_count`, `candidate_pages`, `proposed`, `verified`, `discarded(reason,tier,score)`, `no_result`. pg_trgm phrase index = first fast-follow if replay shows recall misses.

### 8.4 Open-question final resolutions
1. **Pricing**: dedicated quote-search debit, `reason="quote_search"`, predebit = balanced-mode estimate (15), reconcile to actual tokens, refund on system failure, charge actual cost on verified-empty results; recorded job-style (`UsageRecord.message_id=None`), surfaced in chat UX when routed from chat. (Synthesis of r1 job-accounting + r2 chat-style reconcile.)
2. **Caps**: count active saved quotes per user across documents. `FREE_SAVED_QUOTES_LIMIT=30` (r1: 20 risks cutting off thesis users pre-habit), `PLUS_…`/`PRO_…` unlimited-by-default constants in config.
3. **Chat routing: YES in v1** (both rounds concur; overrides Claude's defer position). Strict direct-quote intents only ("direct quote/verbatim/exact quotation/quote with page") — the `action_planner.py:218-225` CITATION_LOOKUP hook already exists; verified-pipeline failure returns "no verified quotes found", never unverified fallback text.
4. **Biblio**: separate table keyed **`(document_id, user_id)`** with a system row for auto-detected defaults — a user's edit must never mutate metadata for demo/shared docs (r2 catch: `Document.user_id` nullable, demo docs shared).
5. **Thresholds**: 95/90 stand + 8.1 guards.

### 8.5 Scope re-cut: the "First Paid Loop" milestones (replaces §5)
The first paid moment = verified quote **discovery → save → jump → copy (in-text citation + page)**. Everything else defers.
- **M0 (ship immediately, decoupled)**: funnel fixes §3 (Codex: SHIP) — incl. config change for FREE 25→50MB (config.py:156 still 25).
- **M1 — substrate**: parse fidelity fixes (8.1) + offset-preserving normalizer + `quote_verification_service` with real-PDF fixtures (multi-page, RTL/CJK, OCR, repeated phrases) — TDD, no UI until green.
- **M2 — loop**: quote-search endpoint (8.4.1 billing + 8.3 telemetry) + chat-intent routing + quote cards (8.2 approximate highlight; copy = quote + "(Author, Year, p. X)" APA in-text best-effort from a minimal user-editable metadata form seeded by filename/PyMuPDF metadata — NO Crossref/citeproc in v1) + academic demo doc + i18n for all new copy (11 locales).
- **M3 — retention + charge**: saved_quotes CRUD (D8 amended: + `source_chunk_id`, offsets, hashes, `verification_score`+verifier version, nullable bboxes, indexes, access control via `can_access_document` pattern, idempotent saves) + caps + trust labels + **in-prod replay vs the retained-academic query corpus (bas\*\*\*/mel\*\*\*/ric\*\*\*/mca\*\*\*) as acceptance gate** → enable Plus gating.
- **Fast-follow (post-validation only)**: citeproc-py full styles (MLA/Chicago) + golden Zotero tests, DOCX quote-bank export (then BibTeX/RIS), Crossref/OpenLibrary enrichment, pg_trgm, span-to-bbox precision mapper, collection-wide search, programmatic SEO tool pages.

### 8.6 Added risk register entries (amends §6)
Chunk-text mutation corrupting displayed quotes (8.1); hard-hyphen loss; page-attribution error on spanning chunks; same-page duplicate collapse; user-edited biblio leaking across users on shared/demo docs; verified-empty paid searches (UX: show count + what was scanned); fuzzy over-match on short phrases.

## 9. Implementation log

### M1 substrate — IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-13, TDD, pending Codex review)
Greenfield + one targeted parse fix; 37 new tests, all green; no regressions (6 unrelated pre-existing failures confirmed via stash: summary-routing / RetainPDF-sidecar / OCR-languages — env/config, not touched by this work). ruff clean. `rapidfuzz==3.13.0` added to requirements.

- **`app/services/text_normalizer.py`** (D2) — offset-preserving normalizer. Per-code-point fold (NFKC + invisible-char drop + quote/dash/ellipsis + CJK width/corner-quote fold + whitespace collapse); `fuzzy=True` adds casefold + Mn-strip. Returns `(norm, norm_to_raw)`; `raw_span()` projects a normalized span back to raw offsets so the displayed slice is always verbatim source. Tests: `tests/test_text_normalizer.py` (17).
- **`app/services/quote_verification_service.py`** (D1) — `verify_quote(proposed, source_text, *, text_quality, parse_method)` → `QuoteVerification(status, display_text, raw_start, raw_end, score, reason)`. Tiers exact→normalized→aligned(rapidfuzz `partial_ratio_alignment`); guards: min 40 chars/8 tokens, length-ratio band, low-quality/OCR cap fuzzy→flagged; exact/normalized always trusted. **Display is always the raw source slice.** Tests: `tests/test_quote_verification_service.py` (12).
- **`app/services/parse_service.py`** `_split_into_sentences` fix (Codex r2 §8.1) — ASCII `.` is a boundary only when followed by whitespace/EOS; kills `U.S.`→`U. S.`, `3.14`→`3. 14`, `e.g.`→`e. g.` corruption while preserving real-boundary and CJK splitting. Tests: `tests/test_parse_sentence_fidelity.py` (8).

**Next (not yet done):** Codex review of the substrate → then M1 remaining (PDF page-text persistence forward-only + saved-quote verification anchors are M3-adjacent) → M2 (quote-search endpoint + retrieval candidate expansion + chat-intent routing + quote-card UI). Caller of `verify_quote` must pass the cited chunk text ± retrieved neighbours (cross-chunk quotes); single-chunk verification is the unit boundary.

### M2 integration surface (scouted 2026-06-13, read-only — for fast execution after substrate review)
- Two existing routing layers detect citation intent today, both too broad for the verified pipeline:

# Backend Conventions

## Async Safety
- **MinIO calls MUST use `asyncio.to_thread()`** in async endpoints. MinIO client is sync (urllib3). Direct calls block event loop; when MinIO is unreachable, blocks ALL requests for 30+s. Client configured with short timeouts (connect=5s, read=10s, 2 retries)
- **Celery uses sync DB** (`psycopg`), API uses async (`asyncpg`). Never mix.

## Credits & Billing
- **Two-stage debit**: ① Pre-check balance (402 if insufficient) → ② `debit_credits()` pre-debits estimated cost (returns ledger ID) → stream → `reconcile_credits()` UPDATEs same ledger entry to actual cost. Single ledger record per chat. LLM failure → DELETE entry + full refund
- **`ChatRequest` exposes only `mode` field** (`quick`/`balanced`; legacy `thorough` is retired). `model` field removed — prevents billing bypass
- Stripe webhook: `checkout.session.completed` for subscriptions only updates plan (no credits); `invoice.payment_succeeded` grants monthly credits (idempotent by invoice.id)
- `POST /api/billing/cancel` is self-serve and records optional `cancel_reason`, `cancel_feedback`, and `refund_requested` metadata in `plan_transitions`. `refund_requested` is an internal review flag; do not issue Stripe refunds from this path unless an explicit refund workflow is added.

## Parse Worker
- `time_limit=600`, `soft_time_limit=540`, `autoretry_for=(Exception,)`, max 2 retries, 60s backoff
- Idempotent re-parse: **delete Qdrant vectors (by `document_id` filter) BEFORE deleting DB pages/chunks**. Ordering matters — a Qdrant outage must leave the existing rows intact (set error + return), else the two stores diverge / data is lost. Then re-index.
- **OCR trigger = `detect_scanned` (no text layer) OR `detect_low_quality_text` (PDF text layer present but garbled — broken-font cmap, Unicode-aware quality score)**. R2b fix for docs like U13 that have garbage text and so were never detected as "scanned".
- **OCR language is content-based**: `detect_script_osd` runs `tesseract --psm 0` (OSD) on sample pages → `resolve_ocr_languages(locale, script)` returns a NARROW set (script family, ≤3, **no `eng` for non-Latin** — it injects Latin noise). Never the kitchen-sink set (causes cross-script hallucination); locale only refines within a script family. Adopt a low-quality re-OCR only if it beats the text-layer quality. Persist `parse_version`/`parse_method`/`text_quality`/`ocr_languages` on the doc.
- Backfill stale/low-quality docs with `scripts/find_low_quality_docs.py` (skips `parse_version>=current` unless `--force`).

## Auth
- **`FOR UPDATE` lock** on verification tokens to prevent TOCTOU
- Internal Auth Adapter API uses `X-Adapter-Secret` header

## Error Handling
- Use `HTTPException` (not `JSONResponse`) for all non-SSE endpoints
- Lifespan pattern (`@asynccontextmanager`) instead of deprecated `@app.on_event`

## Demo System
- 3 seed PDFs auto-deployed at startup from `backend/seed_data/`. Self-healing: detects Qdrant data loss → full re-seed
- Anonymous: 5 msgs/session, 500 sessions/doc, 10 req/min/IP, forced DeepSeek V4 Flash
- Logged-in users accessing demo docs use their credits with no message limit

# Frontend Conventions

## Architecture
- **All pages are `"use client"`** — client components with server wrapper for metadata
- Pages that fetch API data must render meaningful content in loading AND error states (prevents Google Soft 404)

## API Proxy
- **ALL** frontend→backend calls go through `/api/proxy/*` route, which injects JWT. Including SSE chat stream (`sse.ts`). Missing this = 401 errors
- **JWT double-layer**: Auth.js uses encrypted JWE (unreadable by backend). Proxy creates plain HS256 JWT via `jose`. Backend `deps.py` validates exp/iat/sub
- `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking: true` enables cross-provider auto-linking by email
- **Proxy maxDuration**: `route.ts` exports `maxDuration = 60` (Vercel Hobby limit). SSE chat 60s timeout, others 30s

## UI Design System
- **Palette (app UI)**: zinc monochrome + blue accent (`#1D4ED8`/`#60A5FA`). Zero `gray-*`/`indigo-*`/`violet-*`/`purple-*` classes (except Google OAuth brand + status colors). Zero `transition-all` (use specific properties)
- **Editorial marketing layer**: the entire public marketing surface (unauthenticated `/`, `use-cases/*`, `compare/*`, `alternatives/*`, `features/*`, `tools/*`, `pricing`, `trust`, `demo`) uses a SEPARATE scoped editorial design system — `frontend/src/app/editorial.css` (every rule under `.dt-editorial`), a warm-paper palette (`--ed-paper`/`--ed-ink`/`--ed-signal` terracotta `#b0472f`/`--ed-ochre`) with Newsreader serif + IBM Plex Mono fonts, **light-only**. It does NOT use the zinc/blue app palette. **Design decision locked 2026-05-20**: the product runs on TWO surface treatments (editorial marketing terracotta+warm-paper vs functional app zinc+blue) sharing one token base (logo, body font Inter, spacing scale, micro-interactions). A blue-accent unification was tried and reverted because the warm-paper terracotta identity is load-bearing. Do not re-propose merging the accents. Marketing pages compose the shared editorial kit in `frontend/src/components/marketing/` (`MarketingShell`, `EditorialMarketingHeader`, `EdPageHero`, `EdSection`, `EdProse`, `EdFeatureList`, `EdCardGrid`, `EdStepRow`, `EdFaqList`, `EdCtaBanner`, `EdComparisonTable`, `EdInlineCell`, `EdRelatedLinks`, `EdCheckList`, `EdChoiceList`) — `MarketingShell` supplies the `.dt-editorial` root, so kit components never add it themselves. Keep editorial styles scoped under `.dt-editorial`; do not let them leak into the functional app UI, and do not apply the zinc/blue rule to editorial components. Pages still on the zinc/blue app palette: `about`, `contact`, `imprint`, `privacy`, `terms`, `blog/*`, `document-diff` (not yet editorialized).
- **i18n**: Components using `t()` MUST be inside `<LocaleProvider>`. Outside = raw key fallback. Only `en` is statically loaded; other 10 locales lazy-loaded

## PDF & Documents

For each doc row (only called with `Document`s that already have `demo_slug` set): looks up its seed spec by slug; `stat_object(bucket, doc.storage_key)`; on `minio.error.S3Error` with `code == "NoSuchKey"` → reads the local seed PDF and `put_object`s it to **exactly** `doc.storage_key` (id- and key-preserving, DB row untouched) and logs `demo_seed.file_restored`; any other `S3Error` code (e.g. transient `AccessDenied`) is treated as "not missing" (re-raised into the per-doc `except Exception`) so a transient error never triggers a spurious re-upload; unknown slug → skipped + logged, no crash; any other exception per-doc is caught so one bad doc never blocks startup.

Docs that got deleted-and-recreated by the Qdrant branch already get a fresh MinIO upload in the existing create path, so they're correctly excluded from `healthy_docs`.

## B2: Verification-source selector with honest trust labels

**Implemented** in new `backend/app/services/quote_source_service.py`:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class QuoteSource:
    text: str                 # verification corpus, passed to verify_quote(proposed, text)
    kind: str                 # "page_text" | "extracted_text"
    page_start: int
    page_end: int

async def build_quote_source(
    db: AsyncSession, document_id: uuid.UUID, chunk: Chunk, neighbor_chunks: list[Chunk],
) -> QuoteSource
```

Rule exactly as specified: one `Page` query for `page_start..page_end`; if **every** page in range has a row AND non-null/non-blank `.content` → concatenate (page-number order, `\n`-joined) → `kind="page_text"`. Otherwise → dedup `[chunk, *neighbor_chunks]` by `.id`, sort by `(page_start, chunk_index)` ("document order"), join with `\n\n` → `kind="extracted_text"`. Sorting is done explicitly in Python rather than relying solely on the query's `ORDER BY`, so behavior doesn't depend on a driver honoring it.

**TDD evidence:**
```

       -> collection error: ModuleNotFoundError: app.services.quote_source_service
GREEN: python3 -m pytest tests/test_quote_source_service.py -v
       -> 6 passed (single-page complete→page_text; multi-page complete,
          out-of-order rows→page_text sorted correctly; any missing page→
          extracted_text with chunk+neighbor in document order; zero Page
          rows at all→extracted_text; neighbors passed out of order→still
          sorted; cited chunk accidentally duplicated in neighbor_chunks→
          not repeated)
```

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class QuoteCard:
    display_text: str   # server-side raw slice from verify_quote — never the LLM emission
    page: int            # "best page" derived from the cited chunk's own bbox distribution
    page_end: int         # chunk.page_end (full cited-chunk range)
    bboxes: list[dict]    # cited chunk's bboxes, FILTERED to `page`
    tier: str             # "exact" | "normalized" | "aligned"
    source_kind: str      # "page_text" | "extracted_text"  (== QuoteSource.kind)
    chunk_id: str
    score: float

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class QuoteSearchResult:
    cards: list[QuoteCard]
    proposed: int                       # raw LLM proposal count, pre-verification/pre-dedup
    verified: int                       # == len(cards), i.e. POST-dedup count
    discarded: list[tuple[str, str, float]]   # (reason, tier, score) — tier="n/a" for ref_out_of_range
    scanned_chunks: int                 # total chunks the deterministic term scan examined
    usage: tuple[int, int]              # (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens), repair-retry included
    model: str

async def quote_search(db, *, document, user, topic: str, locale: str) -> QuoteSearchResult
```

Flow implemented exactly per brief: `_build_candidates` = `corrective_retrieval_service.retrieve_single(topic, route, document.id, top_k=16, db=db, doc_pages=document.page_count)` (route from `QueryRouter().route(topic, is_collection=False)` — this IS "the existing hybrid stack": dense + lexical + RRF fusion) merged with `_term_scan_candidates` (pure function: normalizes the topic via `text_normalizer.normalize`, splits into ≥3-char terms, scans every chunk's normalized text for the full phrase or any term), deduped by chunk id, capped at 24 (matches `corrective_retrieval_service`'s own non-collection ceiling). One `AsyncOpenAI` call to the balanced model (`settings.MODE_MODELS["balanced"]`) with a data-boundary system prompt (topic + excerpts explicitly framed as untrusted data, abstention licensed via `{"quotes": []}`), JSON-parsed with the same fence-strip + regex-fallback + one repair-retry pattern as `extraction_service.py`, using `AsyncOpenAI`/`await` (chat_service.py's async client pattern) rather than extraction_service's sync `OpenAI` client, since this whole service is async.

Per-proposal disposition: `source_ref_n` int-coerced and range-checked against `len(candidates)` → `("ref_out_of_range", "n/a", 0.0)` on failure (covers hallucinated refs, non-numeric refs, and empty quote text) → `_neighbor_chunks` (chunk_index ±1) → `build_quote_source` (B2) → `verify_quote(text_quality=document.text_quality, parse_method=document.parse_method)` (M1) → only `.verified` survives as a card; everything else → `(verification.reason or "not_located", verification.status, verification.score)` in `discarded`.

**Design decision flagged for Codex review — dedup signature asymmetry:** §8.1's key is `(document_id, normalized_quote_text, page_range, offset-or-bbox-signature)`. I implemented the offset component as `f"{raw_start}-{raw_end}"` **only** for `kind="page_text"` (those offsets are stable — relative to the per-document page-text corpus regardless of which candidate chunk led to the match). For `kind="extracted_text"` the signature is `""` (omitted), because the verification corpus differs per originating chunk (chunk ± its own neighbours), so raw offsets from chunk A's corpus and chunk B's corpus aren't comparable — and the required test ("duplicate quote in overlapping chunks → one card") specifically needs the SAME real occurrence, found via two overlapping candidate chunks, to collapse. Using `chunk_id` as the extracted_text signature (a literal reading of "bbox-signature") would have broken that required behavior. The accepted tradeoff: a genuinely repeated short phrase within one page of a chunk-fallback (no-page-text) document could theoretically over-collapse into one card instead of two. I judge this an acceptable, documented simplification for v1 (verified via the mutation test below that dedup logic is real, not vacuous) but it's a deliberate deviation from a literal reading of the locked spec text worth a second pair of eyes.

**`user` parameter is currently unused inside `quote_search`** — kept for interface parity with the brief's exact signature; access control (`can_access_document`) and billing (predebit/reconcile, §8.4.1) are assumed to be the caller's (B4/B5 endpoint's) responsibility, matching the `run_extraction_job_sync` precedent where the job-runner also doesn't re-check access. Worth confirming this assumption explicitly with whoever implements B4/B5.

python3 -m pytest tests/test_quote_search_service.py -v
-> 8 passed:

**Implemented:** `POST /api/documents/{document_id}/quote-search` in new `backend/app/api/quotes.py`, registered in `main.py`. `require_auth` (401 for anonymous — v1 is the paid wedge), `can_access_document` for ownership, `auth_chat_limiter` reuse for rate limiting, `doc.status == "ready"` gate (409). ## B5: Strict chat-intent routing — the riskiest task, done last

**Implemented:** `ChatAction.VERIFIED_QUOTE_SEARCH` (new enum member, added to `uses_rag_answer_path`) + `_STRICT_QUOTE_RE`/`_STRICT_QUOTE_WITH_PAGE_RE` in `action_planner.py` — a matcher DELIBERATELY SEPARATE from the broad `_CITATION_RE`. Triggers ONLY on unambiguous direct-quote language: EN "direct quote(s)", "exact quotation(s)", "verbatim", "word for word", "quote ... page" (bounded 60-char window, either order); ZH 逐字引用/原文引用/一字不差; ES cita textual/copia tal cual/textualmente. Bare "quote"/"citation"/"source" never match. Checked FIRST in `deterministic_plan` at confidence 0.88 (bypasses the LLM re-classification).

`chat_service.chat_stream` gates the routing (the planner has no auth/doc context to do this itself): fires only when AUTHED + non-demo + single-document (`document_id is not None and not is_collection_session and doc is not None and not doc.demo_slug`). Anonymous/demo/collection sessions fall through to the untouched normal RAG path even when the strict intent matched — a deliberate graceful degradation, not an error. When gated in, `_run_verified_quote_search` (a plain awaitable, NOT a generator — see cancellation-safety note below) runs B3's `quote_search`, persists the assistant `Message`, and reconciles the **CALLER's own chat predebit** (the SAME `debit_credits(reason="chat", ...)` call every RAG-path message already makes) to the quote call's actual token cost — there is no separate quote-search debit, so this cannot double-bill. Verified results become a `ChatArtifact`-shaped SSE `artifact` event (`artifact_type="quote_search"`, `preview.cards`, `citations` built in the same shape `_citation_payload` uses elsewhere, with `focus_snippet` = the exact verified quote so the existing chunk-highlight mechanism highlights precisely the quoted text) + a short intro token. A verified-empty result yields the honest "no verified quotes found (scanned N passages)" message in all 11 product locales — never an unverified fallback answer.

**Cancellation-safety finding (self-review, fixed before commit):** my first draft made `_verified_quote_stream` an async generator that reconciled credits and THEN yielded events. A client disconnect injected at the LAST yield (after `reconcile_credits` had already committed) would have hit the outer setup handler's `except asyncio.CancelledError` branch, which checks `not settled` before running a FULL refund — since nothing in my first draft ever set `settled = True`, that refund would have fired ON TOP OF an already-correct reconcile, double-refunding the user. Fixed by restructuring into `_run_verified_quote_search` — a plain `async def` that does ALL DB work (search, persist, reconcile, record_usage, commit) and returns a `_VerifiedQuoteOutcome`; the caller sets `settled = True` immediately after it returns and BEFORE yielding anything, mirroring the exact `settled` guard pattern already used at 6+ other sites in this file for the identical race. Verified via `agen.athrow(asyncio.CancelledError())` injected right after the "token" event (same technique as `test_asst0_cancellation_baseline.py`) — and via **mutation testing**: temporarily removing the `settled = True` line made the new cancellation test fail exactly as expected, then restored.

**Regression found and fixed en route:** the FULL suite (not just my new test file) surfaced 4 pre-existing tests in `test_chat_setup_refunds.py`/`test_asst0_cancellation_baseline.py` that mock `action_planner.plan` with a minimal `SimpleNamespace(uses_rag_answer_path=True)` lacking an `.action` attribute — my new gate read `action_plan.action` unconditionally. Fixed defensively (`getattr(action_plan, "action", None)`) rather than touching every pre-existing test fixture — real `ActionPlan` always has `.action`, so this is purely a test-double compatibility fix, zero production behavior change. A SECOND regression (self-caught, not from CI): during the cancellation-safety refactor I mis-scoped an `old_string` edit and accidentally spliced my new `_VerifiedQuoteOutcome` dataclass INTO THE MIDDLE of the pre-existing `_CitationRepairResult` dataclass, stripping its `prompt_tokens`/`output_tokens`/`applied` fields — caught by re-running the full suite (3 failures in unrelated citation-repair/summary-routing tests), diagnosed via `git show <pre-session-commit>:...` to recover the original field list, fixed.

**One pre-existing test intentionally updated:** `test_planner_citation_lookup_stays_rag_path` asserted `"这句话在哪页，有没有原文引用？"` (roughly "what page is this on, is there an original-text citation?") routes to `CITATION_LOOKUP`. `原文引用` is one of the brief's REQUIRED strict ZH triggers, so this message now reclassifies to `VERIFIED_QUOTE_SEARCH` — both actions sit in `uses_rag_answer_path`, so this is a routing refinement (arguably more correct — the user did ask about 原文引用), not a path change. Split into two tests: the original assertion narrowed to a phrase without 原文引用, plus a new test documenting the reclassification explicitly.

## B6: Minimal biblio + APA in-text formatter

**Implemented:** `document_biblio` table (migration `20260802_0034`, model `DocumentBiblio` in `tables.py`). **Design deviation from a literal reading of §8.4 point 4** ("PK (document_id, user_id)"): Postgres requires every PRIMARY KEY column NOT NULL, but the system row's `user_id` is NULL by design — so uniqueness is enforced with two partial unique indexes instead (`uq_document_biblio_system` on `document_id WHERE user_id IS NULL`, `uq_document_biblio_user` on `(document_id, user_id) WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL`), functionally equivalent to the intended composite-PK semantics without a synthetic system-user row or a nullable-PK hack. Verified via a **scratch-DB round-trip** (`doctalk_biblio_scratch`, created/dropped on the SAME Postgres server but an isolated database — the shared `doctalk` dev DB was never touched, confirmed by checking `document_biblio` doesn't exist there and `documents` row count is unchanged before/after): `upgrade head` (full chain, 34 migrations) → `downgrade -1` (table cleanly dropped) → `upgrade head` (reapplied) → manual `INSERT` tests confirming the partial indexes actually enforce "one system row per document" and "one row per document+user" (both duplicate-insert attempts correctly raised `duplicate key value violates unique constraint`).

`biblio_service.py`: `get_or_seed_system_biblio` (seeds from filename heuristics — "Author - Title (Year).ext" pattern + bare 4-digit year — enriched with best-effort PyMuPDF `doc.metadata` when a PDF/converted-PDF is available, never raises); `get_biblio_for_user` (read-only: the user's own row if present, else the seeded system default — never creates a user row); `upsert_user_biblio` (always writes the CALLING user's own row, source="user"; never reads or mutates the system row or another user's row); `format_apa_intext(biblio, page) -> str` — pure, no citeproc: "(Family, Year, p. X)", 2 authors → "A & B", 3+ → "A et al.", missing author falls back to title, missing year → "n.d.", missing page omits the fragment.

**Interface:**
```python
async def get_biblio_for_user(db, document, user) -> DocumentBiblio  # .csl_json, .source ("system"|"user")
async def upsert_user_biblio(db, document, user, csl_json: dict) -> DocumentBiblio
def format_apa_intext(biblio: dict, page: int | None) -> str
```
`GET/PUT /api/documents/{id}/biblio` in `quotes.py` (same router as B4), response `{"csl_json": dict, "source": "system"|"user"}`, `PUT` body `{"csl_json": dict}` (20KB cap against pathological payloads, `400 BIBLIO_TOO_LARGE`).

## Fix round 1 (post-review)

Verdict: Spec ✅, Needs fixes — 2 should-fix + 2 minor. `f394b11` (the two carry-in review follow-ups from the B1/B0-B3 gate) was independently re-reviewed clean, nothing to do there.

**SHOULD-FIX-1 — ES strict-quote regex lacked word-boundary anchors.** The alternation `cita\s+textual|copia\s+tal\s+cual|textualmente` had no `\b` anchors, so it matched as a bare substring inside larger words/phrases: "Contextualmente, ¿qué significa...?" matched `textualmente` (inside "Con**textualmente**"), and "Según cita textualidad del informe" matched `cita textual` (as a prefix of "cita **textual**idad"). Both are ordinary interpretive Spanish questions that would have been silently rerouted into the quote pipeline and answered with the verified-empty honesty message instead of a real answer. Fixed by wrapping each alternative in `\b`: `\bcita\s+textual\b|\bcopia\s+tal\s+cual\b|\btextualmente\b`. Verified directly against the reviewer's exact three false-positive examples (all now `False`) and the three original true-positive examples (all still `True`) before touching tests. Added 4 ES cases to `TestStrictQuoteMatcherNegatives` (the negative list previously had zero ES coverage): the two reviewer-demonstrated false positives, plus `"cita esta fuente, por favor"` and `"¿Cuál es la fuente de esta cita?"` (bare "cita" mentions that must stay on the normal path).

**SHOULD-FIX-2 — `_run_verified_quote_search` cancellation asymmetry (the mirror-image race).** The original fix (this wave's initial commit) only handled a CancelledError landing AFTER everything completed (setting `settled = True` once the whole call returned, before any yield). It did NOT handle a CancelledError landing BETWEEN the message-persist commit and the final credits commit — that case fell through to the setup-phase handler's blanket `_settle_predebit_on_cancel(has_answer=False, ...)`, issuing a FULL refund for an answer that was already durably persisted and delivered to the user — a free ride at DocTalk's expense, verified by the reviewer to not double-refund but flagged as the exact mirror of the race already hardened.

Two candidate fixes were on the table: (a) derive `has_answer` from actual persistence evidence, or (b) reorder so the message-persist commit happens only after reconcile. I chose (a) and rejected (b) after tracing what (b) would actually do: if billing (reconcile_credits, which UPDATEs the ledger row's `delta` to `-actual_cost`) ran BEFORE the message persist, and a cancellation then struck before the persist commit, the setup-phase handler's blanket `_settle_predebit_on_cancel(has_answer=False, ...)` would call `_refund_predebit`, which unconditionally adds back the FULL `pre_debited` (15) to the user's balance as long as the ledger row still exists — it doesn't check whether the row was already reconciled to a smaller `actual_cost` first. Reordering would therefore have let a late cancellation delete an already-correctly-reconciled ledger row and refund the full predebit ON TOP of the already-settled reconcile, an over-refund bug in the opposite direction. Option (a) has no such trap: it adds a mutable `_VerifiedQuoteProgress` (populated with `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens`/`model` as soon as `quote_search()` returns, and `message_id` only once the message-persist commit actually succeeds) plus a dedicated `except asyncio.CancelledError` wrapped around the call site in `chat_stream`, which derives `has_answer=quote_progress.message_id is not None` and calls the SAME existing `_settle_predebit_on_cancel` helper used everywhere else in this file (shielded, with the existing `_CANCEL_IO_TIMEOUT_S` timeout), setting `settled = True` before re-raising so the outer setup handler's `not settled` check correctly no-ops. This exactly mirrors the main RAG path's own `has_partial_answer` discriminator (the streaming-phase `finally:` block, chat_service.py) — just derived from persistence instead of accumulated stream text, since this branch has no incremental streaming to inspect.

New regression test: `test_cancellation_between_persist_and_reconcile_settles_as_delivered` forces `credit_service.reconcile_credits` to raise `asyncio.CancelledError` directly (simulating exactly the gap between the two commits), then asserts `_settle_predebit_on_cancel` was called with `has_answer=True` and the REAL token counts (not zeros) — proving the reconcile-not-refund path fires with accurate billing data. Verified via mutation testing (forcing `has_answer=False` back in) that both this NEW test and the EXISTING `test_late_cancellation_after_reconcile_does_not_double_refund` test catch a regression of either half of this now-symmetric guard.

**MINOR-3 — artifact payload hand-built inline.** `_run_verified_quote_search` now constructs a `ChatArtifact` (imported from `chat_tool_executor.py`) and calls `.to_payload()`, identical to every other tool-action artifact in this file, instead of hand-building a dict that could silently drift from the shared shape.

**MINOR-4 — misleading `_refund_predebit` docstring in `quotes.py`.** Corrected from "Mirrors chat_service._refund_predebit exactly" (false — the chat_service version does its own internal `try: await db.rollback() except: pass` before the delete; this one doesn't, because its one caller already rolls back separately right before calling it) to an honest description of the actual difference.

## Wave F (frontend) review fix round

Three MEDIUM findings surfaced by the Wave F review, all backend-side, fixed in one commit.

**1. `quote_search_submitted` missing from `ALLOWED_EVENTS`.** The Quote Finder panel fires this event on submit (client-triggered via `POST /api/events`) but it 400'd — never allowlisted. Added it to `events.py`'s `ALLOWED_EVENTS` set, deliberately NOT to `PUBLIC_EVENTS` (authed only, matching the rest of the quote-search surface). The reviewer noted a suggestion to instead reuse `quote_search_completed` client-side — rejected by the controller: B4's endpoint already records `quote_search_completed` SERVER-SIDE on completion, so a client-side `quote_search_completed` on mere submission would double-count that event name and conflate the submitted/completed funnel stages into one bucket. Keeping the distinct name preserves the funnel semantics. Tests: authed POST accepted (204), anonymous POST rejected (401, not silently recorded) — mutation-tested by reverting the allowlist entry and confirming it reproduces the exact reported 400.

**2. Quote-search chat artifact `status="completed"` → `"succeeded"`.** Every other artifact producer in `chat_tool_executor.py` (extraction, table scan, document diff, question template) uses `status="succeeded"`; the frontend's `ChatArtifactCard` `isDone` check looks for that exact value. `"completed"` isn't recognized, so the card was stuck showing a permanently-neutral "still working" badge even after a successful quote search. One-line fix in `_run_verified_quote_search`; no test had asserted the old value, so nothing needed inverting — added a fresh assertion (`artifact["data"]["status"] == "succeeded"`) to the existing happy-path test to lock it in.

**3. Chat artifact preview missing `discarded_count`.** The REST endpoint (B4) already returns `discarded_count: len(result.discarded)`; the chat artifact's `preview` dict didn't, so the frontend was re-deriving it client-side as `proposed - verified`. That's wrong whenever §8.1 dedup collapses multiple verified duplicates (from overlapping chunks) into one card: those collapsed duplicates count against `verified` being lower than the raw verified count, but they are NOT in `discarded` (they were correctly verified, just deduplicated) — so `proposed - verified` overcounts the true discard rate. Added `"discarded_count": len(result.discarded)` to the preview dict, mirroring the REST response exactly. Updated the existing happy-path test's fixture to `proposed=3, verified=1, discarded=[one entry]` — deliberately a case where `proposed - verified` (=2) and `len(discarded)` (=1) diverge — and asserted `preview["discarded_count"] == 1`, so a regression back to the naive frontend-style calculation would fail this test.

**Evidence:**
```
python3 -m pytest tests/test_quote_intent_routing.py tests/test_events_api.py -v  -> 38 passed
python3 -m pytest -q                    -> 636 passed / 8 skipped (was 634)
python3 -m ruff check app/ tests/       -> clean
SKIP_INTEGRATION=0 python3 -m pytest -m integration -q  -> identical pre-existing baseline, unchanged
```

## F1: Quote Finder panel UI

**Implemented:** `frontend/src/components/Quotes/{QuoteFinderPanel,QuoteCardList,QuoteResultCard,utils}.tsx`, API client additions in `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` (`searchDocumentQuotes`, `QuoteCard`/`QuoteSearchResult` types, plus `getDocumentBiblio`/`DocumentBiblio` types — needed here because Copy already requires biblio), `frontend/src/lib/apaFormat.ts` (pure `formatApaInText`, mirrors `biblio_service.py::format_apa_intext` exactly — same family-name/`n.d.`/`n.a.` rules), and wiring into `DocumentReaderPageClient.tsx`: a "Quotes" toolbar row (always rendered next to the view toggle, previously only rendered for non-PDF docs with a converted PDF — now `.dt-view-toggle` wraps a `justify-between` row so plain single-format PDFs also get the entry point).

Each card shows a "Verified" badge, tier label (exact/normalized/aligned), and the honest trust label from plan §8.1 (page text vs extracted text — never overstates confidence). Jump builds the same `Citation` shape `navigateToCitation`/`onCitationClick` already consume (`citationFromQuoteCard` in `Quotes/utils.ts`) and closes the panel so the highlighted page is visible; an "approximate" note sits next to the page number per §8.2 (bboxes are the cited chunk's, not the exact quote span). - Results summary: `"{verified} verified · {discarded} discarded"` using the endpoint's `verified`/`discarded_count` directly.
- Verified-empty: an explicit honesty line ("scanned {n} passages... try a more specific topic"), not a generic empty state.
- 402 → `PaywallModal` (owned inside `QuoteFinderPanel`, not plumbed up); 401 → `openAuthModal()` + close panel; other errors → `errorCopy(err, t, tOr)`.

**Implemented:** `frontend/src/components/Quotes/BiblioForm.tsx` — authors as one "Family, Given" per line (parsed on first comma per line; no-comma line = family-only, matching the backend seed heuristic's fallback), year, title. ## F3: Chat quote-card artifact rendering

**Implemented:** Modified `ChatArtifactCard.tsx` to render `artifact_type === 'quote_search'` (see "contract correction" below) using the same `QuoteCardList` from F1/F2, with `allowEditBiblio` left off (default `false`) so chat stays "jump + copy identical" to the panel without also exposing the edit surface there. `quoteCardsFromArtifact()` merges the artifact's raw `preview.cards` (snake_case: `ref_index`/`display_text`/`page`/`page_end`/`tier`/`source_kind`/`score` — `mapArtifactPayload` passes `preview` through untransformed for every artifact type) with the already-mapped `citations` array (camelCase `chunkId`/`bboxes`, matched by `ref_index`) to reconstruct the same `QuoteCard` shape F1 gets directly from the endpoint. `documentId` comes from the store (`useDocTalkStore((s) => s.documentId)`) — safe because B5 gates this chat routing to non-collection, single-document, authed, non-demo sessions only, so a `quote_search` artifact never appears without a live `documentId` in the store. The generic download/citation-pill footer is suppressed for this artifact type (each card already renders its own Jump button; showing the same pages again as pills would be redundant). Also widened `ChatArtifact.artifactType`'s union to include `'quote_search'` and added a `QuoteCardsArtifactPreview` type in `types/index.ts` for the raw preview shape.

**Contract correction (flagged per task instructions — code is the contract):** the brief named this "a new artifact type `quote_cards`", but the actual backend wire value (confirmed by reading `chat_service.py::_run_verified_quote_search` directly, not just the wave-b2 report) is `artifact_type: "quote_search"`, matching the same string used by the billed REST endpoint's telemetry (`quote_search_completed`). Implemented against `"quote_search"`, the real value.

**No SSE plumbing changes were needed.** `sse.ts`'s `case 'artifact': onArtifact?.(mapArtifactPayload(data))` already passes any `artifact_type` through generically (confirmed by reading `_tool_action_stream` and `_run_verified_quote_search`, which both just `yield sse("artifact", artifact_payload)` — no `citation` SSE events are emitted for this path, citations only live inside the artifact payload). `useChatStream.ts`'s existing `addArtifactToLastMessage` wiring needed no changes either. The "type plumbing following the existing extraction-artifact pattern exactly" from the brief turned out to already be exact by construction — the only concrete plumbing was the type-union/preview-type addition in `types/index.ts`.

- "verified quote(s)" wording aligned with the backend's own `_QUOTE_SEARCH_FOUND_COPY`/`_QUOTE_SEARCH_EMPTY_COPY` maps in `chat_service.py` (same feature, same user, different surface — e.g. ZH 经核实/引用, JA 検証済み/引用, KO 검증된/인용문, ES cita verificada, DE verifiziert/Zitat, FR citation vérifiée, PT citação verificada, IT citazione verificata, AR اقتباس موثّق, HI सत्यापित/उद्धरण).

## Self-review findings

1. **Reader toolbar is now always visible**, not just for non-PDF docs with a converted PDF. Previously the `.dt-view-toggle` row only rendered when `showViewToggle` was true; now it always renders (view-toggle buttons on the left when applicable, Quote Finder entry on the right). This is an intentional, necessary UI change to give the entry point somewhere to live on plain single-format PDFs (the majority case) — but it is a visible layout change on every document reader page that I have **not** visually verified in a browser (no dev server / auth session set up in this environment). Flagging for the visual-review agent(s) already in this team's roster.
2. **`BiblioForm` doesn't independently re-GET biblio on open** (see F2 design note above) — relies on the parent's already-fetched state. If `QuoteCardList`'s initial GET failed and fell back to `{}`, the form opens with blank fields (correct — not stale data) but does not retry the GET. Acceptable for v1; worth a follow-up if biblio 5xx rates turn out to be non-trivial.
3. **`quoteFinder.page`/`.pageRange` en-dash (`–`) usage**: used the Unicode en-dash consistently in all locales' range key, matching how `en.json`'s own source string was written (`p. {start}–{end}`) — not a hyphen-minus. Confirmed it renders correctly in all 10 translated files (same character copied verbatim into each edit).
4. **Analytics**: quote-panel search fires `quote_search_submitted` (new event name, not registered anywhere else in the frontend event registry — I did not check whether the backend/analytics pipeline has an allowlist for frontend-emitted event names the way `ProductEvent.event_name` has `ALLOWED_EVENTS` on the backend side). Jump/citation clicks reuse the existing `citation_clicked` event untouched. Worth a quick check in the integration wave that arbitrary frontend event names aren't silently dropped or need registration.
5. No backend files were touched. I read but did not modify the concurrent `8239a2c` backend commit; confirmed its wire-contract compatibility with F3 as described above.

## Concerns for Codex review

- Whether showing the toolbar row unconditionally (finding #1) needs a design pass rather than reusing `.dt-view-toggle`'s existing white/bordered styling as-is.
- Whether `quote_search_submitted` (finding #4) needs to be added to any backend/analytics allowlist before it's meaningful in the funnel dashboards.
- The F1↔F2 split left `updateDocumentBiblio` (the PUT function) added to `api.ts` in the F1 commit even though nothing calls it until F2 — a deliberate, disclosed choice to avoid fragmenting one small file edit across two commits (noted here rather than discovered in review).

## 8. Round-2 consensus resolutions (ACCEPTED from Codex r1+r2 — these override conflicting text above)

### 8.1 Verification substrate preconditions (amends D1/D2)
The chunk pipeline is a sound anti-hallucination gate but NOT yet a verbatim-display substrate. Before any quote card renders chunk text:
- **Fix sentence-split mutation**: `_split_into_sentences` (parse_service.py:893-906) + strip/rejoin (:482-487, :765-782) corrupts `U.S.`→`U. S.`, `3.14`→`3. 14`. Chunk display text must come from offset-preserving slices of cleaned block text, or splitting gets abbreviation/decimal guards. Fidelity tests required: `U.S.`, `e.g.`, decimals, DOI strings.
- **Fix hard-hyphen loss**: `_extract_line_blocks` (:855-864) turns `cost-\neffective` into `costeffective`. Mark line-break hyphen joins in an offset map (preserve/restore when ambiguous); tests for discretionary vs compound hyphens.
- **Persist PDF page text forward-only** (`page.get_text("text")` per page) AND store verification anchors on saved quotes: `source_chunk_id`, char offsets, `page_text_hash`, `quote_hash` — saved quotes must survive/revalidate after reparses.
- **Page derivation from the verified slice, not the LLM emission.** For `page_start≠page_end` chunks there is no offset→page map (tables.py:140-145): page-scoped verification where `pages.content` exists; chunk-fallback must reject or split ambiguous multi-page matches.
- **Dedup key**: `(document_id, normalized_quote_text, verified_page_range, start_offset-or-bbox-signature)` — not `(text, page)`.
- **Fuzzy guards**: tier-3 auto-accept additionally requires quote ≥ ~8 tokens / 40 chars, sane length ratio, match within the cited chunk/page window, and clean `text_quality`; short quotes / OCR / `text_quality<0.75` → exact/normalized only or flagged.
- **Honest trust labels**: chunk-fallback docs say "verified against extracted text"; only page-text-verified docs say "verified against page text". Quote Finder misses headings/headers/tables by construction (cleaning strips them) — say so in UI copy.

### 8.2 Highlight (amends D3 — Codex r1 verdict BLOCK accepted)
Persisted bboxes are bare `{page,x,y,w,h}` rects with no offsets/text (parse_service.py:526-530, :936-942) — span-level selection is impossible without reconstruction, and the PDF snippet-fallback only fires on all-dummy bboxes (PageWithHighlights.tsx:64-77).
- v1: emit the cited chunk's bboxes for the verified page, **label highlight precision as approximate**, store `source_chunk_id` + quote span offsets for future precision.
- Frontend change: allow a verified quote to snippet-highlight on the PDF text layer even when bboxes are present-but-coarse (extend, don't bend, the dummy-bbox path).
- Span-to-bbox word mapper (PyMuPDF reopen) = fast-follow, not v1.

### 8.3 Retrieval (amends D4)
Over-retrieve alone is insufficient (24-chunk cap, corrective_retrieval_service.py:92-114; lexical = ILIKE only). v1 adds deterministic candidate expansion: normalized phrase/term scan over the document's chunks (and page text where present) merged into candidates before generation. Telemetry per search: `retrieved_count`, `candidate_pages`, `proposed`, `verified`, `discarded(reason,tier,score)`, `no_result`. pg_trgm phrase index = first fast-follow if replay shows recall misses.

### 8.4 Open-question final resolutions
1. **Pricing**: dedicated quote-search debit, `reason="quote_search"`, predebit = balanced-mode estimate (15), reconcile to actual tokens, refund on system failure, charge actual cost on verified-empty results; recorded job-style (`UsageRecord.message_id=None`), surfaced in chat UX when routed from chat. (Synthesis of r1 job-accounting + r2 chat-style reconcile.)
2. **Caps**: count active saved quotes per user across documents. `FREE_SAVED_QUOTES_LIMIT=30` (r1: 20 risks cutting off thesis users pre-habit), `PLUS_…`/`PRO_…` unlimited-by-default constants in config.
3. **Chat routing: YES in v1** (both rounds concur; overrides Claude's defer position). Strict direct-quote intents only ("direct quote/verbatim/exact quotation/quote with page") — the `action_planner.py:218-225` CITATION_LOOKUP hook already exists; verified-pipeline failure returns "no verified quotes found", never unverified fallback text.
4. **Biblio**: separate table keyed **`(document_id, user_id)`** with a system row for auto-detected defaults — a user's edit must never mutate metadata for demo/shared docs (r2 catch: `Document.user_id` nullable, demo docs shared).
5. **Thresholds**: 95/90 stand + 8.1 guards.

### 8.5 Scope re-cut: the "First Paid Loop" milestones (replaces §5)
The first paid moment = verified quote **discovery → save → jump → copy (in-text citation + page)**. Everything else defers.
- **M0 (ship immediately, decoupled)**: funnel fixes §3 (Codex: SHIP) — incl. config change for FREE 25→50MB (config.py:156 still 25).
- **M1 — substrate**: parse fidelity fixes (8.1) + offset-preserving normalizer + `quote_verification_service` with real-PDF fixtures (multi-page, RTL/CJK, OCR, repeated phrases) — TDD, no UI until green.
- **M2 — loop**: quote-search endpoint (8.4.1 billing + 8.3 telemetry) + chat-intent routing + quote cards (8.2 approximate highlight; copy = quote + "(Author, Year, p. X)" APA in-text best-effort from a minimal user-editable metadata form seeded by filename/PyMuPDF metadata — NO Crossref/citeproc in v1) + academic demo doc + i18n for all new copy (11 locales).
- **M3 — retention + charge**: saved_quotes CRUD (D8 amended: + `source_chunk_id`, offsets, hashes, `verification_score`+verifier version, nullable bboxes, indexes, access control via `can_access_document` pattern, idempotent saves) + caps + trust labels + **in-prod replay vs the retained-academic query corpus (bas\*\*\*/mel\*\*\*/ric\*\*\*/mca\*\*\*) as acceptance gate** → enable Plus gating.
- **Fast-follow (post-validation only)**: citeproc-py full styles (MLA/Chicago) + golden Zotero tests, DOCX quote-bank export (then BibTeX/RIS), Crossref/OpenLibrary enrichment, pg_trgm, span-to-bbox precision mapper, collection-wide search, programmatic SEO tool pages.

### 8.6 Added risk register entries (amends §6)
Chunk-text mutation corrupting displayed quotes (8.1); hard-hyphen loss; page-attribution error on spanning chunks; same-page duplicate collapse; user-edited biblio leaking across users on shared/demo docs; verified-empty paid searches (UX: show count + what was scanned); fuzzy over-match on short phrases.

# Backend Conventions

## Async Safety
- **MinIO calls MUST use `asyncio.to_thread()`** in async endpoints. MinIO client is sync (urllib3). Direct calls block event loop; when MinIO is unreachable, blocks ALL requests for 30+s. Client configured with short timeouts (connect=5s, read=10s, 2 retries)
- **Celery uses sync DB** (`psycopg`), API uses async (`asyncpg`). Never mix.

## Credits & Billing
- **Two-stage debit**: ① Pre-check balance (402 if insufficient) → ② `debit_credits()` pre-debits estimated cost (returns ledger ID) → stream → `reconcile_credits()` UPDATEs same ledger entry to actual cost. Single ledger record per chat. LLM failure → DELETE entry + full refund
- **`ChatRequest` exposes only `mode` field** (`quick`/`balanced`; legacy `thorough` is retired). `model` field removed — prevents billing bypass
- Stripe webhook: `checkout.session.completed` for subscriptions only updates plan (no credits); `invoice.payment_succeeded` grants monthly credits (idempotent by invoice.id)
- `POST /api/billing/cancel` is self-serve and records optional `cancel_reason`, `cancel_feedback`, and `refund_requested` metadata in `plan_transitions`. `refund_requested` is an internal review flag; do not issue Stripe refunds from this path unless an explicit refund workflow is added.

## Parse Worker
- `time_limit=600`, `soft_time_limit=540`, `autoretry_for=(Exception,)`, max 2 retries, 60s backoff
- Idempotent re-parse: **delete Qdrant vectors (by `document_id` filter) BEFORE deleting DB pages/chunks**. Ordering matters — a Qdrant outage must leave the existing rows intact (set error + return), else the two stores diverge / data is lost. Then re-index.
- **OCR trigger = `detect_scanned` (no text layer) OR `detect_low_quality_text` (PDF text layer present but garbled — broken-font cmap, Unicode-aware quality score)**. R2b fix for docs like U13 that have garbage text and so were never detected as "scanned".
- **OCR language is content-based**: `detect_script_osd` runs `tesseract --psm 0` (OSD) on sample pages → `resolve_ocr_languages(locale, script)` returns a NARROW set (script family, ≤3, **no `eng` for non-Latin** — it injects Latin noise). Never the kitchen-sink set (causes cross-script hallucination); locale only refines within a script family. Adopt a low-quality re-OCR only if it beats the text-layer quality. Persist `parse_version`/`parse_method`/`text_quality`/`ocr_languages` on the doc.
- Backfill stale/low-quality docs with `scripts/find_low_quality_docs.py` (skips `parse_version>=current` unless `--force`).

## Auth
- **`FOR UPDATE` lock** on verification tokens to prevent TOCTOU
- Internal Auth Adapter API uses `X-Adapter-Secret` header

## Error Handling
- Use `HTTPException` (not `JSONResponse`) for all non-SSE endpoints
- Lifespan pattern (`@asynccontextmanager`) instead of deprecated `@app.on_event`

## Demo System
- 3 seed PDFs auto-deployed at startup from `backend/seed_data/`. Self-healing: detects Qdrant data loss → full re-seed
- Anonymous: 5 msgs/session, 500 sessions/doc, 10 req/min/IP, forced DeepSeek V4 Flash
- Logged-in users accessing demo docs use their credits with no message limit

# Frontend Conventions

## Architecture
- **All pages are `"use client"`** — client components with server wrapper for metadata
- Pages that fetch API data must render meaningful content in loading AND error states (prevents Google Soft 404)

## API Proxy
- **ALL** frontend→backend calls go through `/api/proxy/*` route, which injects JWT. Including SSE chat stream (`sse.ts`). Missing this = 401 errors
- **JWT double-layer**: Auth.js uses encrypted JWE (unreadable by backend). Proxy creates plain HS256 JWT via `jose`. Backend `deps.py` validates exp/iat/sub
- `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking: true` enables cross-provider auto-linking by email
- **Proxy maxDuration**: `route.ts` exports `maxDuration = 60` (Vercel Hobby limit). SSE chat 60s timeout, others 30s

## UI Design System
- **Palette (app UI)**: zinc monochrome + blue accent (`#1D4ED8`/`#60A5FA`). Zero `gray-*`/`indigo-*`/`violet-*`/`purple-*` classes (except Google OAuth brand + status colors). Zero `transition-all` (use specific properties)
- **Editorial marketing layer**: the entire public marketing surface (unauthenticated `/`, `use-cases/*`, `compare/*`, `alternatives/*`, `features/*`, `tools/*`, `pricing`, `trust`, `demo`) uses a SEPARATE scoped editorial design system — `frontend/src/app/editorial.css` (every rule under `.dt-editorial`), a warm-paper palette (`--ed-paper`/`--ed-ink`/`--ed-signal` terracotta `#b0472f`/`--ed-ochre`) with Newsreader serif + IBM Plex Mono fonts, **light-only**. It does NOT use the zinc/blue app palette. **Design decision locked 2026-05-20**: the product runs on TWO surface treatments (editorial marketing terracotta+warm-paper vs functional app zinc+blue) sharing one token base (logo, body font Inter, spacing scale, micro-interactions). A blue-accent unification was tried and reverted because the warm-paper terracotta identity is load-bearing. Do not re-propose merging the accents. Marketing pages compose the shared editorial kit in `frontend/src/components/marketing/` (`MarketingShell`, `EditorialMarketingHeader`, `EdPageHero`, `EdSection`, `EdProse`, `EdFeatureList`, `EdCardGrid`, `EdStepRow`, `EdFaqList`, `EdCtaBanner`, `EdComparisonTable`, `EdInlineCell`, `EdRelatedLinks`, `EdCheckList`, `EdChoiceList`) — `MarketingShell` supplies the `.dt-editorial` root, so kit components never add it themselves. Keep editorial styles scoped under `.dt-editorial`; do not let them leak into the functional app UI, and do not apply the zinc/blue rule to editorial components. Pages still on the zinc/blue app palette: `about`, `contact`, `imprint`, `privacy`, `terms`, `blog/*`, `document-diff` (not yet editorialized).
- **i18n**: Components using `t()` MUST be inside `<LocaleProvider>`. Outside = raw key fallback. Only `en` is statically loaded; other 10 locales lazy-loaded

## PDF & Documents
- **react-pdf v9 CJK**: After upgrading react-pdf/pdfjs-dist, MUST re-copy `cmaps/`, `standard_fonts/`, `pdf.worker.min.mjs` to `public/`. Worker loaded from same-origin (not CDN) for CSP compliance
- **bbox coordinates**: Normalized [0,1], top-left origin. Three citation highlight strategies: ① PDF bbox, ② TextViewer text-snippet match, ③ converted PDF fallback to text-snippet when dummy bbox detected

## Subscriptions & Feature Gating
- Free (300/mo) + Plus (3K/mo, $9.99) + Pro (9K/mo, $19.99). Annual = 20% discount
- Visible modes are Flash and Pro. Internal IDs remain `quick` and `balanced`; retired modes such as `thorough` must migrate to Flash.
- Free includes Flash plus a capped number of Pro answers/month. Export: Plus+ (frontend gated). Custom Instructions: Pro (backend gated). Sessions: Free=3/doc (backend gated)
- Credit packs: Boost(500/$3.99), Power(2K/$9.99), Ultra(5K/$19.99)
- Cancellation UI must remain self-serve. The cancel form may collect an optional reason, optional feedback, and a refund-review checkbox, but it must not block cancellation on those fields.
