    25	
    26	from app.models.tables import Document, DocumentBiblio, User
    27	
    28	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    29	
    30	SYSTEM_SOURCE = "system"
    31	USER_SOURCE = "user"
    32	
    33	_EXTENSION_RE = re.compile(r"\.(pdf|docx?|pptx?|xlsx?|txt|md)$", re.IGNORECASE)
    34	_YEAR_RE = re.compile(r"(?:\(((?:19|20)\d{2})\)|\b((?:19|20)\d{2})\b)")
    35	_AUTHOR_TITLE_SPLIT_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*([^-–—:]{2,60})\s*[-–—:]\s*(.+)$")
    36	
    37	
    38	def _split_author_name(name: str) -> Optional[dict[str, str]]:
    39	    name = name.strip()
    40	    if not name:
    41	        return None
    42	    parts = name.split()
    43	    if len(parts) == 1:
    44	        return {"family": parts[0], "given": ""}
    45	    return {"family": parts[-1], "given": " ".join(parts[:-1])}
    46	
    47	
    48	def _seed_csl_from_filename(filename: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    49	    """Filename heuristics (D6 seed step 1): "Author - Title (Year).ext" or
    50	    "Author: Title.ext" style filenames yield an author + title guess; a bare
    51	    4-digit year anywhere is picked up too. Falls back to the filename itself
    52	    as the title when nothing else parses — always returns SOMETHING so the
    53	    system row is never blocked on this heuristic failing."""

    88	async def _enrich_from_pdf_metadata(document: Document, csl: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    89	    """Best-effort enrichment (D6 seed step 1, PyMuPDF doc metadata) — opens
    90	    the document's PDF (or its converted-to-PDF representation for
    91	    DOCX/PPTX) and fills in author/title/year from PyMuPDF's metadata dict
    92	    where the filename heuristic didn't already find them. NEVER raises —
    93	    any failure (storage unavailable, corrupt file, non-PDF with no
    94	    conversion yet) just keeps the filename-only seed."""
    95	    try:
    96	        file_type = getattr(document, "file_type", "pdf") or "pdf"
    97	        storage_key = document.storage_key
    98	        if file_type != "pdf":
    99	            converted = getattr(document, "converted_storage_key", None)
   100	            if not converted:
   101	                return csl
   102	            storage_key = converted
   103	
   104	        import fitz
   105	
   106	        from app.services.storage_service import storage_service
   107	
   108	        data = await asyncio.to_thread(storage_service.download_file, storage_key)
   109	        pdf_doc = fitz.open(stream=data, filetype="pdf")
   110	        try:
   111	            meta = pdf_doc.metadata or {}
   112	        finally:
   113	            pdf_doc.close()
   114	
   115	        pdf_title = (meta.get("title") or "").strip()
   116	        if pdf_title and not csl.get("author"):
   117	            # Only override the filename-guessed title when we don't already
   118	            # have a confident author+title split — a real PDF title field
   119	            # is usually more reliable than the filename by itself.
   120	            csl["title"] = pdf_title
   121	        elif pdf_title and not csl.get("title"):
   122	            csl["title"] = pdf_title
   123	
   124	        pdf_author = (meta.get("author") or "").strip()
   125	        if pdf_author and not csl.get("author"):
   126	            names = re.split(r"[;,&]| and ", pdf_author)
   127	            authors = [a for a in (_split_author_name(n) for n in names) if a]
   128	            if authors:

   130	
   131	        creation = meta.get("creationDate") or ""
   132	        year_match = re.match(r"D:(\d{4})", creation)
   133	        if year_match and not csl.get("issued"):
   134	            csl["issued"] = {"year": int(year_match.group(1))}

   136	        logger.info("biblio PDF metadata enrichment skipped for %s: %s", getattr(document, "id", None), exc)

   140	async def _fetch_system_row(db: AsyncSession, document_id: uuid.UUID) -> Optional[DocumentBiblio]:
   141	    result = await db.execute(
   142	        select(DocumentBiblio)
   143	        .where(DocumentBiblio.document_id == document_id)
   144	        .where(DocumentBiblio.user_id.is_(None))
   145	    )
   146	    return result.scalar_one_or_none()
   147	
   148	
   149	async def _fetch_user_row(
   150	    db: AsyncSession, document_id: uuid.UUID, user_id: uuid.UUID
   151	) -> Optional[DocumentBiblio]:
   152	    result = await db.execute(
   153	        select(DocumentBiblio)
   154	        .where(DocumentBiblio.document_id == document_id)
   155	        .where(DocumentBiblio.user_id == user_id)
   156	    )
   157	    return result.scalar_one_or_none()

   159	
   160	async def get_or_seed_system_biblio(db: AsyncSession, document: Document) -> DocumentBiblio:
   161	    """Return the document's system (auto-detected default) row, seeding it
   162	    from filename heuristics + best-effort PyMuPDF metadata on first access."""
   163	    existing = await _fetch_system_row(db, document.id)
   164	    if existing:
   165	        return existing
   166	
   167	    csl = _seed_csl_from_filename(document.filename)
   168	    csl = await _enrich_from_pdf_metadata(document, csl)
   169	    row = DocumentBiblio(document_id=document.id, user_id=None, csl_json=csl, source=SYSTEM_SOURCE)
   170	    db.add(row)
   171	    await db.commit()
   172	    return row
   173	
   174	
   175	async def get_biblio_for_user(db: AsyncSession, document: Document, user: User) -> DocumentBiblio:
   176	    """The effective biblio for GET: the user's own edit if they have one,
   177	    else the (seeded) system default. Never creates a user row — read-only
   178	    fallback."""
   179	    user_row = await _fetch_user_row(db, document.id, user.id)
   180	    if user_row:
   181	        return user_row
   182	    return await get_or_seed_system_biblio(db, document)
   183	
   184	
   185	async def upsert_user_biblio(
   186	    db: AsyncSession, document: Document, user: User, csl_json: dict[str, Any]
   187	) -> DocumentBiblio:
   188	    """PUT: always writes to the CALLING user's own row (source='user'),
   189	    creating it if needed. Never reads or mutates the system row or any
   190	    other user's row — that's the whole point of the per-user key."""
   191	    existing = await _fetch_user_row(db, document.id, user.id)
   192	    if existing:
   193	        existing.csl_json = csl_json
   194	        existing.source = USER_SOURCE
   195	        await db.commit()
   196	        return existing
   197	
   198	    row = DocumentBiblio(document_id=document.id, user_id=user.id, csl_json=csl_json, source=USER_SOURCE)
   199	    db.add(row)
   200	    await db.commit()
   201	    return row

   204	def format_apa_intext(biblio: dict[str, Any], page: Optional[int]) -> str:
   205	    """Pure function: minimal APA in-text citation, no citeproc (§8.5).
   206	
   207	    "(Family, Year, p. X)"; 2 authors -> "A & B"; 3+ -> "A et al.";
   208	    missing author falls back to title; missing year -> "n.d."; missing
   209	    page omits the page fragment entirely.
   210	    """
   211	    authors = biblio.get("author") or []
   212	    families = [
   213	        a.get("family", "").strip()
   214	        for a in authors
   215	        if isinstance(a, dict) and (a.get("family") or "").strip()
   216	    ]
   217	    if families:
   218	        if len(families) == 1:
   219	            who = families[0]
   220	        elif len(families) == 2:
   221	            who = f"{families[0]} & {families[1]}"
   222	        else:
   223	            who = f"{families[0]} et al."
   224	    else:
   225	        title = (biblio.get("title") or "").strip()
   226	        who = title if title else "n.a."
   227	
   228	    year = (biblio.get("issued") or {}).get("year")
   229	    year_str = str(year) if year else "n.d."
   230	
   231	    page_str = f", p. {page}" if page else ""
   232	    return f"({who}, {year_str}{page_str})"

   716	        .order_by(PageModel.page_number)

    49	def _set_doc_error(doc, code: str, human: str | None = None) -> None:
    50	    """Mark a Document as errored with a structured ERR_CODE prefix.
    51	
    52	    Wire contract (transitional bridge — full taxonomy is frontend/Phase 3):
    53	        doc.error_msg = "ERR_CODE:<CODE>:<human text>"
    54	    Idempotent: repeated calls on an already-prefixed message do NOT stack
    55	    additional ERR_CODE: prefixes. Legacy free-text rows written before
    56	    this migration remain readable by consumers that fall back to the raw
    57	    string when no ERR_CODE: prefix is present.
    58	    """
    59	    text = human if human is not None else _WORKER_ERROR_CODES.get(code, "Document processing failed")
    60	    payload = text if text.startswith("ERR_CODE:") else f"ERR_CODE:{code}:{text}"
    61	    doc.status = "error"
    62	    doc.error_msg = payload

    66	    from urllib.parse import urlparse
    67	    endpoint = settings.MINIO_ENDPOINT
    68	    access_key = settings.MINIO_ACCESS_KEY
    69	    secret_key = settings.MINIO_SECRET_KEY
    70	    # Parse endpoint for scheme-based secure detection
    71	    if endpoint.startswith("http://") or endpoint.startswith("https://"):
    72	        parsed = urlparse(endpoint)
    73	        secure = parsed.scheme == "https"
    74	        host = parsed.netloc
    75	    else:
    76	        host = endpoint
    77	        secure = bool(settings.MINIO_SECURE)
    78	    return Minio(host, access_key=access_key, secret_key=secret_key, secure=secure)

     """Two-tier, PDF-scoped detector for a present-but-garbled (broken-font) text layer that
     detect_scanned() misses (it only checks for *absence* of text). Returns
     (needs_ocr, quality_score). Calibrated in-prod: U13 garbage lnm=0.56 vs good docs ≥0.94.
     """
     q = text_quality_score(pages)
     if file_type != "pdf":
         return False, q  # only PDFs have broken-font layers and are OCR-able via fitz
     if q >= 0.75:
         return False, q  # clearly good (good docs ≥0.94 — wide margin)
     if q < 0.50:
         return True, q   # clear garbage incl. no-space U+FFFD/PUA runs (CJK-safe: good CJK ≥0.9)
     # ambiguous 0.50–0.75: require a second, script-robust garbage signal
     return (_bad_char_ratio(pages) > 0.30 or _avg_token_len(pages) < 4.0), q

    28	function useDesktopReaderLayout() {

    31	  useEffect(() => {
    32	    if (typeof window === 'undefined') return;

    34	    const sync = () => setIsDesktopLayout(media.matches);
    35	    sync();
    36	    media.addEventListener('change', sync);
    37	    return () => media.removeEventListener('change', sync);
    38	  }, []);
    39	
    40	  return isDesktopLayout;
    41	}

     6	/**

    12	 * quote's page (§8.2 v1 decision) — highlight location is approximate,
    13	 * not the exact quote span; see `approxHighlightLabel` below.

    15	export function citationFromQuoteCard(card: QuoteCard, documentId: string, index: number): Citation {
    16	  return {
    17	    refIndex: card.refIndex ?? index + 1,
    18	    chunkId: card.chunkId,
    19	    page: card.page,
    20	    pageEnd: card.pageEnd,
    21	    bboxes: card.bboxes || [],
    22	    textSnippet: card.displayText,
    23	    focusSnippet: card.displayText,
    24	    offset: 0,
    25	    documentId,
    26	  };
    27	}

    30	  if (tier === 'exact') return tOr('quoteFinder.tier.exact', 'Exact match');
    31	  if (tier === 'normalized') return tOr('quoteFinder.tier.normalized', 'Normalized match');
    32	  if (tier === 'aligned') return tOr('quoteFinder.tier.aligned', 'Close match');
    33	  return tier;

    43	    : tOr('quoteFinder.trust.extractedText', 'Verified against extracted text');

     1	import type { DocumentBiblioCsl } from './api';
     2	
     3	/**
     4	 * Minimal APA in-text citation formatter — mirrors
     5	 * `backend/app/services/biblio_service.py::format_apa_intext` exactly
     6	 * (same family-name rules, same "n.d."/"n.a." fallbacks, same page
     7	 * fragment behavior) so the clipboard text the user gets from the Quote
     8	 * Finder panel and the chat quote-card artifact matches what the backend
     9	 * would produce for the same biblio + page. No citeproc-py, no
    10	 * Crossref/DOI lookup in M2 (plan §8.5) — this stays a pure, dependency-free
    11	 * function.
    12	 */
    13	export function formatApaInText(biblio: DocumentBiblioCsl | null | undefined, page: number | null | undefined): string {
    14	  const authors = biblio?.author || [];
    15	  const families = authors
    16	    .map((a) => (a?.family || '').trim())
    17	    .filter((f) => f.length > 0);
    18	
    19	  let who: string;
    20	  if (families.length === 1) {
    21	    who = families[0];
    22	  } else if (families.length === 2) {
    23	    who = `${families[0]} & ${families[1]}`;
    24	  } else if (families.length >= 3) {
    25	    who = `${families[0]} et al.`;
    26	  } else {
    27	    const title = (biblio?.title || '').trim();
    28	    who = title || 'n.a.';
    29	  }
    30	
    31	  const year = biblio?.issued?.year;
    32	  const yearStr = year ? String(year) : 'n.d.';
    33	  const pageStr = page ? `, p. ${page}` : '';
    34	  return `(${who}, ${yearStr}${pageStr})`;
    35	}

frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:818:  "useCasesHub.cases.finance.description": "Analyze 10-K filings, earnings reports, and investor presentations with AI. Extract key metrics and verify figures with citations pointing to original tables.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:865:  "useCasesFinance.docTypes.pdf10K.detail": "SEC annual and quarterly reports from EDGAR or company investor relations pages. Handles complex multi-column layouts, financial tables, and footnotes.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:867:  "useCasesFinance.docTypes.xlsxModels.detail": "Upload spreadsheets with financial models, budget comparisons, and data tables. Ask questions about specific data points across sheets and columns.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:899:  "useCasesFinance.faq.q2.answer": "Yes. DocTalk supports XLSX file uploads. You can upload financial models, budget spreadsheets, and data tables, then ask questions about the data.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:900:  "useCasesFinance.faq.q3.question": "How does DocTalk handle financial tables and numbers?",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:901:  "useCasesFinance.faq.q3.answer": "DocTalk extracts text from tables in PDF, DOCX, and XLSX documents and converts them to a structured format. When you ask about specific figures, the AI locates the relevant table and cites the exact location.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1125:  "featuresDemo.docs.doc2.description": "Explore how DocTalk handles structured content like sections, headings, and data — with cited answers throughout.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1306:  "featuresMultiFormat.formatTxtDesc": "Plain text and markdown rendering with full formatting support. Markdown tables, code blocks, and headings are preserved.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1312:  "featuresMultiFormat.whyPara2": "With a PDF-only tool, you are forced to convert every document to PDF first — losing formatting, breaking tables, and adding friction to every analysis. With DocTalk, you upload the original file and start chatting immediately.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1318:  "featuresMultiFormat.howStep2Desc": "The document is parsed asynchronously using format-specific extractors. Text, tables, headings, and metadata are extracted and indexed for semantic search.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1325:  "featuresMultiFormat.detailDocxText": "Body element iteration extracts paragraphs and tables in their natural reading order — not as separate lists. Heading hierarchy is preserved for context.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1331:  "featuresMultiFormat.detailTxtText": "Markdown is rendered with full formatting: tables (remark-gfm), code blocks, headings, and lists. Plain text files are displayed with preserved whitespace.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1351:  "featuresMultiFormat.faq1A": "Yes. DocTalk fully supports Microsoft Word (.docx) files. It extracts paragraphs, tables, and heading structure while preserving the document layout for accurate AI analysis. Citations link back to specific sections of the document.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1419:  "compareChatpdf.feature.formatSupportP2Pre": "DocTalk natively supports seven formats: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, TXT, Markdown, and web URLs. Each format is parsed with a dedicated extractor that preserves the document structure, including tables, headings, and paragraph breaks. For example, the XLSX parser preserves spreadsheet structure, and the PPTX parser maintains slide order with speaker notes. This means you can upload your files directly without any conversion step, and the AI receives clean, structured text that produces better answers. See our ",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1613:  "altsChatpdf.alt1Desc1": "DocTalk is the most comprehensive ChatPDF alternative, addressing every major limitation of ChatPDF while adding features ChatPDF does not have. Where ChatPDF supports only PDF files, DocTalk handles seven formats: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, TXT, Markdown, and web URLs, with dedicated parsers for each format that preserve document structure including tables, headings, and slide layouts.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1643:  "altsChatpdf.alt6Desc1": "ChatDOC differentiates itself with strong table extraction and structured data handling. If your documents are heavy on tables, charts, and structured data, ChatDOC better preserves those structures during analysis. The tool supports PDF and DOCX files with particular attention to tabular content.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1716:  "altsNotebooklm.alt6Desc1": "Elicit is an AI research assistant designed specifically for systematic literature reviews. It helps you find relevant papers, extract key data points, and organize findings into structured tables. Elicit goes beyond simple Q&A to support the entire research workflow, from search to synthesis.",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1934:  "comparePdfai.documentFormatDocTalk": "DocTalk supports seven formats natively: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, TXT, Markdown, and web URLs. Each format has a dedicated parser that preserves the original document structure, including tables, headings, slide order, and spreadsheet cell relationships. This eliminates the conversion step entirely and produces cleaner input for the AI, leading to better answers. See",
frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:2105:  "useCasesStudents.docTypes.pdf.detail": "Papers from arXiv, PubMed, IEEE Xplore, JSTOR, Springer, Elsevier, and any other repository. Handles multi-column layouts, equations, and tables.",

    17	// Detect dummy bboxes (0,0,1,1) used by non-PDF extractors
    18	function isDummyBbox(bbox: NormalizedBBox): boolean {
    19	  return bbox.x === 0 && bbox.y === 0 && bbox.w === 1 && bbox.h === 1;

    22	// Validate bbox values are within expected bounds (allow h=0 for overlay estimation)
    23	function isValidBbox(bbox: NormalizedBBox): boolean {

    25	    typeof bbox.x === 'number' && isFinite(bbox.x) && bbox.x >= 0 && bbox.x <= 1 &&
    26	    typeof bbox.y === 'number' && isFinite(bbox.y) && bbox.y >= 0 && bbox.y <= 1 &&
    27	    typeof bbox.w === 'number' && isFinite(bbox.w) && bbox.w > 0 && bbox.w <= 1 &&
    28	    typeof bbox.h === 'number' && isFinite(bbox.h) && bbox.h >= 0 && bbox.h <= 1
    29	  );
    30	}
    31	
    32	// 矩形相交测试（带容差）— increased tolerance for PyMuPDF/PDF.js coord differences
    33	function bboxOverlap(
    34	  a: { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number },
    35	  b: { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number },
    36	  tol = 0.02
    37	): boolean {
    38	  return (
    39	    a.x < b.x + b.w + tol &&
    40	    a.x + a.w > b.x - tol &&
    41	    a.y < b.y + b.h + tol &&
    42	    a.y + a.h > b.y - tol
    43	  );
    44	}

    46	// HTML 特殊字符转义 - comprehensive escaping for security

    53	    .replace(/'/g, '&#x27;')
    54	    .replace(/\//g, '&#x2F;');
    55	}

    40	async def build_quote_source(
    41	    db: AsyncSession,
    42	    document_id: uuid.UUID,
    43	    chunk: Chunk,
    44	    neighbor_chunks: list[Chunk],
    45	) -> QuoteSource:
    46	    page_start = chunk.page_start
    47	    page_end = chunk.page_end
    48	
    49	    result = await db.execute(
    50	        select(Page)
    51	        .where(Page.document_id == document_id)
    52	        .where(Page.page_number >= page_start)
    53	        .where(Page.page_number <= page_end)
    54	        .order_by(Page.page_number)
    55	    )
    56	    # Sort explicitly rather than relying solely on the query's ORDER BY —
    57	    # cheap, and keeps concatenation order correct regardless of driver/test-
    58	    # double behavior.
    59	    pages = sorted(result.scalars().all(), key=lambda p: p.page_number)
    60	    expected_page_count = page_end - page_start + 1
    61	    all_pages_have_content = (
    62	        len(pages) == expected_page_count
    63	        and all((p.content or "").strip() for p in pages)
    64	    )
    65	
    66	    if all_pages_have_content:
    67	        text = "\n".join(p.content for p in pages)
    68	        return QuoteSource(text=text, kind="page_text", page_start=page_start, page_end=page_end)
    69	
    70	    # Fallback: cited chunk ± neighbours, deduped by chunk id, joined in
    71	    # document order (page_start, then chunk_index) so cross-chunk quotes
    72	    # read as a contiguous excerpt.
    73	    by_id: dict[uuid.UUID, Chunk] = {}
    74	    for c in (chunk, *neighbor_chunks):
    75	        by_id[c.id] = c
    76	    ordered = sorted(by_id.values(), key=_document_order_key)
    77	    text = "\n\n".join((c.text or "") for c in ordered)
    78	    return QuoteSource(text=text, kind="extracted_text", page_start=page_start, page_end=page_end)

   111	### 8.1 Verification substrate preconditions (amends D1/D2)
   112	The chunk pipeline is a sound anti-hallucination gate but NOT yet a verbatim-display substrate. Before any quote card renders chunk text:
   113	- **Fix sentence-split mutation**: `_split_into_sentences` (parse_service.py:893-906) + strip/rejoin (:482-487, :765-782) corrupts `U.S.`→`U. S.`, `3.14`→`3. 14`.     mode: Optional[Literal["quick", "balanced", "thorough"]] = None
    domain_mode: Optional[Literal["legal", "academic"]] = None
    locale: Optional[str] = None  # Frontend locale code (en/zh/es/fr/de)


class ContinueRequest(BaseModel):
    message_id: Optional[str] = None  # If absent, use most recent assistant message
    mode: Optional[Literal["quick", "balanced", "thorough"]] = None
    locale: Optional[str] = None


class ChatMessageResponse(BaseModel):
    id: uuid.UUID
    share_anchor: str
    role: str
    content: str
    citations: Optional[List[dict]] = None
    metadata_json: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)
    created_at: datetime

    class Config:
        from_attributes = True


class SessionResponse(BaseModel):
    session_id: uuid.UUID
    document_id: uuid.UUID
    title: Optional[str] = None
    created_at: datetime


class SessionCreateResponse(SessionResponse):
    demo_messages_used: Optional[int] = None


class SessionMessagesResponse(BaseModel):
    messages: List[ChatMessageResponse]
    demo_messages_used: Optional[int] = None


class SessionListItem(BaseModel):
    session_id: uuid.UUID
    title: Optional[str] = None
    message_count: int
    domain_mode: Optional[str] = None
    created_at: datetime
    last_activity_at: datetime


class SessionListResponse(BaseModel):
    sessions: List[SessionListItem]

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any

from openai import AsyncOpenAI

from app.core.config import settings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class ChatAction(str, Enum):
    ANSWER_WITH_RAG = "answer_with_rag"
    SUMMARIZE_DOCUMENT = "summarize_document"
    EXTRACT_DELIVERABLE = "extract_deliverable"
    SCAN_TABLES = "scan_tables"
    EXPORT_TABLES = "export_tables"
    CREATE_QUESTION_TEMPLATE = "create_question_template"
    RUN_QUESTION_TEMPLATE = "run_question_template"
    COMPARE_DOCUMENTS = "compare_documents"
    CITATION_LOOKUP = "citation_lookup"
    VERIFIED_QUOTE_SEARCH = "verified_quote_search"
    CLARIFY = "clarify"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ActionPlan:
    action: ChatAction
    confidence: float
    requires_confirmation: bool
    missing_slots: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    scope: str = "current_document"
    document_ids: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    artifact_format: str | None = None
    template_key: str | None = None
    user_visible_status: str = ""
    reason: str = ""

    @property
    def uses_rag_answer_path(self) -> bool:
        return self.action in {
            ChatAction.ANSWER_WITH_RAG,
            ChatAction.SUMMARIZE_DOCUMENT,
            ChatAction.CITATION_LOOKUP,
            ChatAction.VERIFIED_QUOTE_SEARCH,
        }


_TABLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(table|tables|csv|excel|spreadsheet|row|rows|column|columns)\b"
    r"|表格|数据表|CSV|Excel|导出表|提取表",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_EXPORT_RE = re.compile(r"\b(export|download|csv|excel|xlsx)\b|导出|下载|CSV|Excel|表格文件", re.IGNORECASE)
_SUMMARY_RE = re.compile(r"\b(summarize|summary|brief|overview|tldr|executive summary)\b|总结|摘要|概括|要点", re.IGNORECASE)
_FACT_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(key facts|figures|metrics|target price|rating|eps|revenue|valuation|facts)\b"
    r"|目标价|评级|收入|估值|利润|指标|关键事实|数字|金额",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_EVIDENCE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(evidence table|clauses?|legal|academic|claims?)\b|证据表|条款|法律|学术|论据", re.IGNORECASE)
_COMPARE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(compare|contrast|diff|difference|version|old version|previous)\b|对比|比较|差异|旧版|上一版|版本", re.IGNORECASE)
_TEMPLATE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(template|checklist|question list|run the same questions)\b|模板|清单|检查清单|同样的问题", re.IGNORECASE)
_CITATION_RE = re.compile(r"\b(where|which page|citation|source|quote|verbatim)\b|在哪页|引用|出处|来源|原文|定位", re.IGNORECASE)
_CJK_RE = re.compile(r"[\u3400-\u9fff]")

# Strict verbatim-quote intent (plan \u00a78.4.3) \u2014 DELIBERATELY SEPARATE from
# _CITATION_RE above. _CITATION_RE is broad ("where/source/quote/verbatim")
# and routes to the ordinary RAG answer path (CITATION_LOOKUP already sits in
# uses_rag_answer_path); it must keep matching ordinary citation-quality
# questions ("where is this discussed?", "what page is this on?") unchanged.
# This matcher is narrow on purpose: only unambiguous direct-quote requests
# ("direct quote", "verbatim", "exact quotation", "word for word", "quote ...
# with page") should route to the verified quote-search pipeline. Bare
# "quote"/"citation"/"source" must NOT match here \u2014 those stay on the normal
# RAG path per the strict-intent-only routing decision (plan \u00a78.4 point 3).
_STRICT_QUOTE_RE = re.compile(
    r"\bdirect\s+quotes?\b"
    r"|\bexact\s+quotations?\b"
    r"|\bverbatim\b"
    r"|\bword[\s-]for[\s-]word\b"
    r"|\u9010\u5b57\u5f15\u7528|\u539f\u6587\u5f15\u7528|\u4e00\u5b57\u4e0d\u5dee"
    r"|\bcita\s+textual\b|\bcopia\s+tal\s+cual\b|\btextualmente\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
# "quote ... with page" / "page ... quote" \u2014 a bounded window so it doesn't
# also fire on unrelated quote-mention-somewhere-near-a-page-mention text.
_STRICT_QUOTE_WITH_PAGE_RE = re.compile(
    r"\bquote\b[^.?!\n]{0,60}\bpage\b|\bpage\b[^.?!\n]{0,60}\bquote\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def _has_strict_quote_intent(text: str) -> bool:
    return bool(_STRICT_QUOTE_RE.search(text)) or bool(_STRICT_QUOTE_WITH_PAGE_RE.search(text))


def _status(query: str, english: str, chinese: str) -> str:
    return chinese if _CJK_RE.search(query or "") else english


def deterministic_plan(message: str, *, is_collection: bool = False) -> ActionPlan:
    text = " ".join((message or "").strip().split())
    if not text:
        return ActionPlan(
            action=ChatAction.ANSWER_WITH_RAG,
            confidence=0.2,
            requires_confirmation=False,
            user_visible_status="",
            reason="empty message",
        )

    has_export = bool(_EXPORT_RE.search(text))
    has_summary = bool(_SUMMARY_RE.search(text))
    has_fact = bool(_FACT_RE.search(text))
    has_evidence = bool(_EVIDENCE_RE.search(text))
    has_compare = bool(_COMPARE_RE.search(text))
    has_template = bool(_TEMPLATE_RE.search(text))
    has_citation = bool(_CITATION_RE.search(text))
    wants_direct_chat_answer = bool(
        re.search(
            r"\b(answer directly|directly in chat|do not start|do not create|no separate)\b"
            r"|直接在聊天|不要启动|不要生成.*任务|不要.*结构化",

     1	"""Offset-preserving text normalization for the Quote Finder verifier (D2).
     2	
     3	The verifier matches an LLM-emitted quote against stored chunk text. Both
     4	sides are normalized with the IDENTICAL pipeline so quote/dash/ligature/width/
     5	whitespace variants align; a parallel index map then projects a match in
     6	normalized space back to RAW source offsets. The displayed quote is always the
     7	raw slice — never the normalized text and never the LLM emission — so the map
     8	must be exact.
     9	
    10	Two levels, selected by ``fuzzy``:
    11	
    12	* base (``fuzzy=False``)  — used by the exact-normalized tier. Folds only what
    13	  copy-paste / PDF extraction routinely varies (NFKC per code point, invisible
    14	  formatting chars, quote/dash/ellipsis, CJK width + corner quotes, whitespace
    15	  runs). Case and diacritics are PRESERVED.
    16	* fuzzy (``fuzzy=True``) — base plus ``casefold`` and combining-mark (Mn)
    17	  stripping (Arabic tashkeel etc.). Used only by the rapidfuzz alignment tier.
    18	
    19	All transforms are per-code-point so ``norm_to_raw[i]`` is the raw index that
    20	produced ``norm[i]``. A single raw code point may expand to several normalized
    21	chars (e.g. the ﬁ ligature → ``fi``, the … ellipsis → ``...``); every emitted
    22	char maps back to that one raw index.
    23	"""
    24	from __future__ import annotations
    25	
    26	import unicodedata
    27	from typing import List, Tuple
    28	
    29	# Punctuation folds applied per code point (after NFKC). NFKC already handles
    30	# full-width forms and NBSP, so this table only covers what NFKC leaves alone:
    31	# curly quotes, dash variants, the ellipsis char, and CJK corner quotes.
    32	_FOLD_MAP = {
    33	    "“": '"',  # “ left double quote
    34	    "”": '"',  # ” right double quote
    35	    "„": '"',  # „ low double quote
    36	    "«": '"',  # « guillemet
    37	    "»": '"',  # »
    38	    "‘": "'",  # ‘ left single quote
    39	    "’": "'",  # ’ right single quote / apostrophe
    40	    "‚": "'",  # ‚
    41	    "′": "'",  # ′ prime
    42	    "–": "-",  # – en dash
    43	    "—": "-",  # — em dash
    44	    "‐": "-",  # ‐ hyphen
    45	    "‑": "-",  # ‑ non-breaking hyphen
    46	    "‒": "-",  # ‒ figure dash
    47	    "―": "-",  # ― horizontal bar
    48	    "…": "...",  # … ellipsis
    49	    "「": '"',  # 「 corner bracket
    50	    "」": '"',  # 」
    51	    "『": '"',  # 『 white corner bracket
    52	    "』": '"',  # 』
    53	}
    54	
    55	# Invisible / decorative code points dropped in every mode.
    56	_DROP = {
    57	    "­",  # soft hyphen
    58	    "ـ",  # Arabic tatweel / kashida
    59	    "﻿",  # zero-width no-break space / BOM
    60	    "​",  # zero-width space
    61	}
    62	
    63	
    64	def _fold_codepoint(ch: str, *, fuzzy: bool) -> str | None:
    65	    """Return the normalized form of a single raw code point.
    66	
    67	    ``None`` signals "this is whitespace" (collapsed by the caller). ``""``
    68	    signals "drop entirely". Otherwise a 1+ char string is returned.
    69	    """
    70	    if ch in _DROP:
    71	        return ""
    72	    if ch.isspace():
    73	        return None
    74	
    75	    # NFKC per code point: folds ligatures (ﬁ→fi), full-width (３→3), NBSP, etc.
    76	    folded = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", ch)
    77	
    78	    out: List[str] = []
    79	    for c in folded:
    80	        if c in _DROP:
    81	            continue
    82	        if c in _FOLD_MAP:
    83	            out.append(_FOLD_MAP[c])
    84	            continue
    85	        if fuzzy and unicodedata.category(c) == "Mn":
    86	            # Combining mark (Arabic tashkeel, residual European accents):
    87	            # stripped only in the fuzzy tier.
    88	            continue
    89	        out.append(c.casefold() if fuzzy else c)
    90	    return "".join(out)
    91	
    92	
    93	def normalize(text: str, *, fuzzy: bool = False) -> Tuple[str, List[int]]:
    94	    """Normalize ``text`` and return ``(norm_text, norm_to_raw)``.
    95	
    96	    ``norm_to_raw[i]`` is the index in ``text`` of the raw code point that
    97	    produced ``norm_text[i]``. Whitespace runs collapse to a single space that
    98	    maps to the first whitespace code point of the run.
    99	    """
   100	    out_chars: List[str] = []
   101	    out_map: List[int] = []
   102	    prev_space = False
   103	
   104	    for raw_i, ch in enumerate(text):
   105	        folded = _fold_codepoint(ch, fuzzy=fuzzy)
   106	        if folded is None:  # whitespace
   107	            if prev_space:
   108	                continue
   109	            out_chars.append(" ")
   110	            out_map.append(raw_i)
   111	            prev_space = True
   112	            continue
   113	        if folded == "":  # dropped
   114	            continue
   115	        prev_space = False
   116	        for c in folded:
   117	            out_chars.append(c)
   118	            out_map.append(raw_i)
   119	
   120	    return "".join(out_chars), out_map
   121	
   122	
   123	def span_on_raw_boundaries(
   124	    norm_to_raw: List[int], norm_start: int, norm_end: int
   125	) -> bool:
   126	    """True iff ``[norm_start, norm_end)`` begins and ends at raw code-point
   127	    boundaries — i.e. the match spans WHOLE raw code points, not part of one
   128	    code point's multi-char expansion (… → ``...``, ﬁ → ``fi``, ㍿ → 株式会社).
   129	
   130	    A normalized match that ends inside an expansion does not correspond to a
   131	    real source substring, so the exact-normalized tier must reject it.
   132	    """
   133	    n = len(norm_to_raw)
   134	    if norm_start >= norm_end or norm_start < 0 or norm_end > n:
   135	        return False
   136	    start_ok = norm_start == 0 or norm_to_raw[norm_start] != norm_to_raw[norm_start - 1]
   137	    end_ok = norm_end == n or norm_to_raw[norm_end] != norm_to_raw[norm_end - 1]
   138	    return start_ok and end_ok
   139	
   140	
   141	def raw_span(
   142	    norm_to_raw: List[int], raw_len: int, norm_start: int, norm_end: int
   143	) -> Tuple[int, int]:
   144	    """Project a half-open normalized span ``[norm_start, norm_end)`` back to a
   145	    half-open RAW span. ``raw_len`` is ``len(original_text)``."""
   146	    if norm_start >= norm_end or not norm_to_raw:
   147	        return (0, 0)
   148	    raw_start = norm_to_raw[norm_start]
   149	    raw_end = norm_to_raw[norm_end - 1] + 1
   150	    return (raw_start, min(raw_end, raw_len))

     1	"""Quote Finder verification gate (D1) — "LLM proposes, verifier disposes,
     2	source displays."
     3	
     4	The LLM only *proposes* a quote string. This service locates that string in the
     5	stored source text (the cited chunk's text, ± retrieved neighbours) and returns
     6	the RAW source slice for display. The LLM emission is never shown. Three tiers:
     7	
     8	1. ``exact``      — exact substring of the raw source.
     9	2. ``normalized`` — exact substring after identical offset-preserving
    10	   normalization (folds quote/dash/ligature/width/whitespace variation),
    11	   projected back to raw offsets.
    12	3. ``aligned``    — rapidfuzz ``partial_ratio_alignment`` locates the best
    13	   window; auto-accepted only above ``auto_cutoff`` AND past the length /
    14	   length-ratio / document-quality guards. ``flagged`` when a fuzzy match is
    15	   credible but a guard withholds auto-accept; ``dropped`` below ``flag_cutoff``
    16	   or when the proposal cannot be located.
    17	
    18	Guards (plan §8.1): short quotes over-match under fuzzy alignment, and a
    19	garbled (OCR / low ``text_quality``) source cannot anchor a verbatim guarantee,
    20	so fuzzy auto-accept is withheld in those cases. Deterministic substring tiers
    21	(exact / normalized) are always trusted regardless of document quality.

    34	FLAG_CUTOFF = 90.0  # below this a fuzzy match is dropped entirely

    44	
    45	@dataclass

.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-02-quote-finder-m2-impl/wave-b1-report.md:131:**Design decision flagged for Codex review — dedup signature asymmetry:** §8.1's key is `(document_id, normalized_quote_text, page_range, offset-or-bbox-signature)`. I implemented the offset component as `f"{raw_start}-{raw_end}"` **only** for `kind="page_text"` (those offsets are stable — relative to the per-document page-text corpus regardless of which candidate chunk led to the match). For `kind="extracted_text"` the signature is `""` (omitted), because the verification corpus differs per originating chunk (chunk ± its own neighbours), so raw offsets from chunk A's corpus and chunk B's corpus aren't comparable — and the required test ("duplicate quote in overlapping chunks → one card") specifically needs the SAME real occurrence, found via two overlapping candidate chunks, to collapse. Using `chunk_id` as the extracted_text signature (a literal reading of "bbox-signature") would have broken that required behavior. The accepted tradeoff: a genuinely repeated short phrase within one page of a chunk-fallback (no-page-text) document could theoretically over-collapse into one card instead of two. I judge this an acceptable, documented simplification for v1 (verified via the mutation test below that dedup logic is real, not vacuous) but it's a deliberate deviation from a literal reading of the locked spec text worth a second pair of eyes.

     1	"""Tests for the billed quote-search endpoint (B4, plan §8.4.1/§8.3).
     2	
     3	Billing mirrors chat_service's two-stage debit exactly (predebit 15,
     4	reason="quote_search", reconcile to actual tokens, DELETE+refund the ledger
     5	row on failure) — see tests/test_extractions_api.py for the established
     6	mocked-db pattern this file follows.
     7	"""
     8	from __future__ import annotations
     9	
    10	import uuid
    11	from types import SimpleNamespace
    12	from unittest.mock import AsyncMock
    13	
    14	import pytest
    15	import pytest_asyncio
    16	from fastapi import FastAPI
    17	from httpx import ASGITransport, AsyncClient

    19	from app.api import quotes as quotes_api
    20	from app.core import deps as deps_module
    21	from app.services import credit_service, quote_search_service
    22	from app.services.quote_search_service import QuoteCard, QuoteSearchResult
    23	
    24	api_app = FastAPI()
    25	api_app.include_router(quotes_api.router)
    26	
    27	
    28	class _Result:
    29	    def __init__(self, *, scalar_one_or_none: object = None, rowcount: int = 0) -> None:
    30	        self._scalar_one_or_none = scalar_one_or_none
    31	        self.rowcount = rowcount
    32	
    33	    def scalar_one_or_none(self):
    34	        return self._scalar_one_or_none
    35	
    36	
    37	def _make_user(*, plan: str = "free") -> SimpleNamespace:
    38	    return SimpleNamespace(id=uuid.uuid4(), plan=plan, email="user@example.com")
    39	
    40	
    41	def _make_doc(user: SimpleNamespace, *, status: str = "ready", demo_slug=None) -> SimpleNamespace:
    42	    return SimpleNamespace(
    43	        id=uuid.uuid4(), user_id=user.id, status=status, demo_slug=demo_slug,
    44	        text_quality=0.95, parse_method="text", page_count=10,
    45	    )
    46	
    47	
    48	def _make_db(**overrides: object) -> SimpleNamespace:
    49	    payload: dict[str, object] = {
    50	        "get": AsyncMock(return_value=None),
    51	        "execute": AsyncMock(return_value=_Result()),
    52	        "add": lambda _obj: None,
    53	        "flush": AsyncMock(),
    54	        "commit": AsyncMock(),
    55	        "refresh": AsyncMock(),
    56	        "rollback": AsyncMock(),
    57	    }
    58	    payload.update(overrides)
    59	    return SimpleNamespace(**payload)
    60	
    61	
    62	def _override_dependencies(db: object, user: object) -> None:
    63	    async def _get_db():
    64	        yield db
    65	
    66	    async def _require_auth():
    67	        return user
    68	
    69	    api_app.dependency_overrides[deps_module.get_db_session] = _get_db
    70	    api_app.dependency_overrides[deps_module.require_auth] = _require_auth
    71	
    72	
    73	def _sample_card(**overrides) -> QuoteCard:
    74	    base = dict(
    75	        display_text="the exact quoted sentence",
    76	        page=4, page_end=4, bboxes=[], tier="exact",
    77	        source_kind="extracted_text", chunk_id=str(uuid.uuid4()), score=100.0,
    78	    )
    79	    base.update(overrides)
    80	    return QuoteCard(**base)
    81	
    82	
    83	def _sample_result(**overrides) -> QuoteSearchResult:
    84	    base = dict(
    85	        cards=[_sample_card()], proposed=1, verified=1, discarded=[],
    86	        scanned_chunks=12, usage=(500, 120), model="deepseek-v4-pro",
    87	    )
    88	    base.update(overrides)
    89	    return QuoteSearchResult(**base)
    90	
    91	
    92	def _assert_error(response, status_code: int, error_code: str) -> dict:
    93	    assert response.status_code == status_code
    94	    body = response.json()
    95	    detail = body["detail"]
    96	    assert detail["error"] == error_code
    97	    return detail

   122	@pytest.mark.asyncio
   123	async def test_quote_search_insufficient_credits_pre_check(
   124	    client: AsyncClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
   125	) -> None:
   126	    """Optimistic pre-check (like chat's) rejects before any debit is attempted."""
   127	    user = _make_user()
   128	    doc = _make_doc(user)
   129	    db = _make_db(get=AsyncMock(return_value=doc))
   130	    _override_dependencies(db, user)
   131	    debit_mock = AsyncMock(return_value=None)
   132	    monkeypatch.setattr(credit_service, "debit_credits", debit_mock)
   133	    monkeypatch.setattr(credit_service, "get_user_credits", AsyncMock(return_value=3))
   134	
   135	    response = await client.post(
   136	        f"/api/documents/{doc.id}/quote-search", json={"topic": "climate risk"}
   137	    )
   138	
   139	    detail = _assert_error(response, 402, "INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS")
   140	    assert detail["required"] == 15
   141	    assert detail["balance"] == 3
   142	    debit_mock.assert_not_awaited()  # pre-check short-circuits before any debit attempt
   143

   145	@pytest.mark.asyncio
   146	async def test_quote_search_debit_race_falls_back_to_402(
   147	    client: AsyncClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
   148	) -> None:
   149	    """Pre-check passes optimistically but the atomic debit_credits() still
   150	    fails (TOCTOU race) — must still surface 402, not a 500."""
   151	    user = _make_user()
   152	    doc = _make_doc(user)

# Adversarial review

Found 3 BLOCKERs, 4 IMPORTANTs, and 3 MINORs.

## BLOCKER

### 1. Extracted-text fallback can render wording that is not verbatim from the document

The locked substrate required hard-hyphen fidelity before any chunk-derived quote card rendered. The parser still unconditionally removes a trailing hyphen when the next line begins with an alphanumeric character: [parse_service.py:885](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/parse_service.py:885). Thus `cost-\neffective` loses the literal `-`.

Legacy PDFs have no `Page.content`, so they fall back to this mutated chunk text plus neighbors: [quote_source_service.py:61](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_source_service.py:61), [quote_source_service.py:70](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_source_service.py:70). An LLM can copy the mutated form, receive an `exact` verification, and have that server slice rendered: [quote_search_service.py:382](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_search_service.py:382), [quote_search_service.py:404](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_search_service.py:404).

The `extracted_text` trust label does not satisfy locked §8.1’s explicit fidelity prerequisite, especially while the UI says results are “word-for-word quotes from this document”: [QuoteFinderPanel.tsx:150](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/frontend/src/components/Quotes/QuoteFinderPanel.tsx:150).

Required: preserve/map ambiguous hard hyphens, backfill page text, or reject extracted-text PDF cards where original fidelity cannot be established.

### 2. Verification can succeed on one page while the card cites and highlights another

For multi-page chunks, the verification corpus concatenates every page: [quote_source_service.py:46](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_source_service.py:46), [quote_source_service.py:66](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_source_service.py:66). Extracted fallback broadens it further with adjacent chunks, potentially from other pages: [quote_source_service.py:70](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_source_service.py:70).

After verification, page and bboxes are not derived from `verification.raw_start/raw_end`; they come from the candidate chunk’s majority bbox page: [quote_search_service.py:302](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_search_service.py:302), [quote_search_service.py:396](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_search_service.py:396). The copied APA citation also trusts this page: [QuoteResultCard.tsx:21](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/frontend/src/components/Quotes/QuoteResultCard.tsx:21).

Targeted reproduction: a quote existing only on page 2 of a page-1–2 source produced:

```text
reported_page=1, page_end=2, bbox_pages=[1,1]
```

The same error reaches REST responses, live chat artifacts, persisted metadata, jump, highlight, and copy. This directly violates locked §8.1’s page-from-verified-slice requirement.

Required: verify page-by-page and derive attribution from the matching page, or discard ambiguous multi-page/neighbor matches.

### 3. Chat can reserve 5 credits for a balanced-model quote search, and reconciliation permits negative balances

Chat pre-checks and predebits according to the user-selected mode: [chat.py:420](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/api/chat.py:420), [chat_service.py:1508](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/chat_service.py:1508). Therefore `mode="quick"` reserves 5 credits.

The strict route nevertheless always invokes Quote Finder’s balanced model: [quote_search_service.py:41](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_search_service.py:41), [chat_service.py:1292](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/chat_service.py:1292), then reconciles using balanced pricing: [chat_service.py:1374](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/chat_service.py:1374).

Reconciliation has no sufficient-balance predicate and freely subtracts an overrun: [credit_service.py:182](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/credit_service.py:182). Targeted calculation showed:

```text
quick predebit=5
required balanced predebit=15
7000 prompt + 1000 output tokens=20 credits
```

Concurrent searches amplify this: each atomic debit can pass, after which each reconciliation may push the account further negative. This bypasses locked §8.4.1’s balanced predebit of 15 and lets accounts consume work beyond their available credits.

## IMPORTANT

### 4. Both billing paths have uncovered post-debit failure windows

REST catches failures only around `quote_search()`: [quotes.py:144](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/api/quotes.py:144). Reconciliation, usage/event insertion, and the final commit are outside that handler: [quotes.py:159](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/api/quotes.py:159), [quotes.py:194](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/api/quotes.py:194). A reconciliation/commit failure leaves the already-committed 15-credit predebit in place. `CancelledError` also bypasses `except Exception`.

Chat has the inverse hole: it commits the verified answer before billing: [chat_service.py:1349](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/chat_service.py:1349), [chat_service.py:1364](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/chat_service.py:1364). An ordinary reconciliation/usage failure then reaches the generic full-refund path: [chat_service.py:1377](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/chat_service.py:1377), [chat_service.py:1920](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/chat_service.py:1920). The persisted artifact remains accessible after reload for free.

Cancellation is not fully proven safe either: `progress.message_id` is assigned only after `commit()` returns: [chat_service.py:1363](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/chat_service.py:1363). The self-heal checks absence and later performs an unconditional overwrite: [demo_seed.py:92](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/demo_seed.py:92), [demo_seed.py:111](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/demo_seed.py:111). ## BLOCKER

### 1. Extracted-text fallback can render wording that is not verbatim from the document

The locked substrate required hard-hyphen fidelity before any chunk-derived quote card rendered. The parser still unconditionally removes a trailing hyphen when the next line begins with an alphanumeric character: [parse_service.py:885](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/parse_service.py:885). Thus `cost-\neffective` loses the literal `-`.

Legacy PDFs have no `Page.content`, so they fall back to this mutated chunk text plus neighbors: [quote_source_service.py:61](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_source_service.py:61), [quote_source_service.py:70](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_source_service.py:70). An LLM can copy the mutated form, receive an `exact` verification, and have that server slice rendered: [quote_search_service.py:382](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_search_service.py:382), [quote_search_service.py:404](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_search_service.py:404).

The `extracted_text` trust label does not satisfy locked §8.1’s explicit fidelity prerequisite, especially while the UI says results are “word-for-word quotes from this document”: [QuoteFinderPanel.tsx:150](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/frontend/src/components/Quotes/QuoteFinderPanel.tsx:150).

Required: preserve/map ambiguous hard hyphens, backfill page text, or reject extracted-text PDF cards where original fidelity cannot be established.

### 2. Verification can succeed on one page while the card cites and highlights another

For multi-page chunks, the verification corpus concatenates every page: [quote_source_service.py:46](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_source_service.py:46), [quote_source_service.py:66](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_source_service.py:66). Extracted fallback broadens it further with adjacent chunks, potentially from other pages: [quote_source_service.py:70](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_source_service.py:70).

After verification, page and bboxes are not derived from `verification.raw_start/raw_end`; they come from the candidate chunk’s majority bbox page: [quote_search_service.py:302](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_search_service.py:302), [quote_search_service.py:396](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_search_service.py:396). The copied APA citation also trusts this page: [QuoteResultCard.tsx:21](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/frontend/src/components/Quotes/QuoteResultCard.tsx:21).

Targeted reproduction: a quote existing only on page 2 of a page-1–2 source produced:

```text
reported_page=1, page_end=2, bbox_pages=[1,1]
```

The same error reaches REST responses, live chat artifacts, persisted metadata, jump, highlight, and copy. This directly violates locked §8.1’s page-from-verified-slice requirement.

Required: verify page-by-page and derive attribution from the matching page, or discard ambiguous multi-page/neighbor matches.

### 3. Chat can reserve 5 credits for a balanced-model quote search, and reconciliation permits negative balances

Chat pre-checks and predebits according to the user-selected mode: [chat.py:420](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/api/chat.py:420), [chat_service.py:1508](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/chat_service.py:1508). Therefore `mode="quick"` reserves 5 credits.

The strict route nevertheless always invokes Quote Finder’s balanced model: [quote_search_service.py:41](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/quote_search_service.py:41), [chat_service.py:1292](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/chat_service.py:1292), then reconciles using balanced pricing: [chat_service.py:1374](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/chat_service.py:1374).

Reconciliation has no sufficient-balance predicate and freely subtracts an overrun: [credit_service.py:182](/Users/mayijie/Projects/Code/010_DocTalk/backend/app/services/credit_service.py:182). Targeted calculation showed:

```text
quick predebit=5
required balanced predebit=15
7000 prompt + 1000 output tokens=20 credits
```

Concurrent searches amplify this: each atomic debit can pass, after which each reconciliation may push the account further negative. This bypasses locked §8.4.1’s balanced predebit of 15 and lets accounts consume work beyond their available credits.
